Separately, and without that time limit, it is unlawful to retaliate because a tenant organized or participated in a tenants' association or lawfully exercised any legal right. Threatening to report a tenant, or anyone the landlord knows to be associated with the tenant, to immigration authorities is retaliatory conduct under both rules. A landlord may still act within the 180 days for a lawful reason if the notice states the good-faith ground relied on, and must prove that ground if it is challenged. A landlord who violates the section is liable for actual damages plus punitive damages of $100 to $2,000 for each retaliatory act involving fraud, oppression or malice, and the court awards attorney's fees to the prevailing party if either party requests them when the action begins. Any waiver of these protections is void.
notes: CA: Civ. Code s1942.5, primary text supplied by Taylor 2026-09-19 (operative 2021-10-01 per s1942.5(l); amended by AB 832, Stats. 2021 ch. 27). Points the library has no analogue for: s1942.5(c) and (e) - THREATENING TO REPORT THE TENANT OR ANYONE ASSOCIATED WITH THE TENANT TO IMMIGRATION AUTHORITIES is expressly retaliatory under both the (a) and (d) prohibitions. No prior state has an immigration-based retaliation provision. s1942.5(k) carves out compliance with federal rent-limitation or rental-assistance program obligations. s1942.5(a)(1) expressly lists NOTICE OF A SUSPECTED BED BUG INFESTATION as a trigger, which ties this directly to bed-bug-disclosure-ca and edu-bed-bug-landlord-duties-ca - a tenant report under that chapter starts a 180-day retaliation clock. TWO DISTINCT PROHIBITIONS, easily collapsed: (a) is the 180-day tenantability window, limited to a tenant not in default on rent and invokable once per 12 months (s1942.5(b)); (d) is a separate, untimed ban on retaliation for tenant organizing or lawfully exercising ANY right, with the burden of producing evidence on the TENANT. Do not merge them. s1942.5(g) is the landlord's safe harbour and it is a DRAFTING duty: the notice must state the good-faith ground relied on, and the landlord must establish its truth if controverted - which dovetails with the s1946.2 just-cause statement requirement. s1942.5(i) is a RECIPROCAL FEE PROVISION triggered by either party requesting fees at initiation - relevant to the default-by-tenant / attorney-fee reciprocity question flagged in the CA extend manifest. s1942.5(f): waiver void as contrary to public policy, independent of s1953. ADDED 2026-09-19: Civ. Code s1942.6 - a person entering on an occupant's invitation, during reasonable hours or in an emergency, to provide information on tenants' rights or to participate in a tenants' association is NOT LIABLE FOR TRESPASS. Complements the s1942.5(d) protection of tenant organising.

title: Owner and Manager Identification
bodyText: Person authorized to manage the premises: {{manager_name}}, {{manager_phone}}, {{manager_street_address}}. Owner, or person authorized to act for the owner for service of process and for receiving and receipting all notices and demands: {{owner_agent_name}}, {{owner_agent_phone}}, {{owner_agent_street_address}}. Rent is payable to {{rent_payee_name}} at {{rent_payee_address}}, {{rent_payee_phone}}, in the following form or forms: {{rent_payment_forms}}. If rent may be paid personally, it may be paid on {{rent_payment_days_hours}}. Landlord will give Tenant a copy of this Lease within 15 days after Tenant signs it, and, once each calendar year on Tenant's request, an additional copy within 15 days.
notes: CA: Civ. Code s1962, primary text supplied by Taylor 2026-09-19 (amended Stats. 2012 ch. 695 (AB 1953)). Sits in CHAPTER 4, Identification of Property Owners - outside the Chapter 2 landlord-tenant provisions. Instruction 7 cross-chapter pattern, fifth confirmation in CA. s1962(a) says 'Disclose THEREIN', so this is content the statute requires IN THE LEASE ITSELF - not a separate notice. The street address must be one 'at which personal service may be effected', so a PO box will not do. s1962(a)(2)(B) gives the owner an ALTERNATIVE to naming a payee: disclose either the financial-institution account number plus the institution's name and street address, PROVIDED THE INSTITUTION IS WITHIN FIVE MILES of the rental property, or the information needed to set up an electronic funds transfer. The five-mile limit is a real constraint the builder must express. ENFORCEMENT TEETH, s1962(c): the duty runs to a SUCCESSOR owner or manager, who must comply within 15 days of succeeding, and a successor who has not complied MAY NOT serve a CCP s1161(2) notice or otherwise evict for nonpayment of rent that accrued during the noncompliance period - though the tenant remains liable for the rent. A missing disclosure therefore disarms the eviction remedy for a period. s1962(d): a party who signs on behalf of a non-complying owner is DEEMED THE OWNER'S AGENT for service of process, for performing the owner's obligations, and for receiving rent - and (d)(3) then allows rent in cash, check, money order or any previously accepted form unless the agreement specifies a form or the tenant was notified in writing. s1962(f): where the disclosed address does not allow personal delivery, mailed rent or notice is CONCLUSIVELY presumed received on the date posted if the tenant proves mailing. s1961 READ 2026-09-19 and the scope gap is CLOSED: Chapter 4 'shall apply to every dwelling structure containing ONE OR MORE UNITS offered to the public for rent or for lease for residential purposes'. No unit-count threshold, no owner-type exemption, no small-landlord carve-out - unlike s1950.5(c)(5) or s1947.12(d). A single rented house is covered. The one boundary in the text is 'offered to the public', which is not defined in s1961 and has not been researched. s1962(b) oral-agreement variant not modelled. RECEIPTS, Civ. Code s1499 read 2026-09-19: 'A debtor has a right to require from his creditor a written receipt for any property delivered in performance of his obligation.' General and ON REQUEST - it covers every rent payment in any form, but it is not an automatic cash-receipt duty of the Minnesota kind.

title: Rent Increase Notice
bodyText: For a tenancy from week to week, month to month, or any period less than a month, Landlord may increase the rent only on written notice delivered to Tenant personally or served by mail under Code of Civil Procedure section 1013. If the increase, by itself or combined with any other increases in the 12 months before its effective date, is 10 percent or less of the rent charged at any time during those 12 months, the notice will be delivered at least 30 days before the increase takes effect. If it is greater than 10 percent, the notice will be delivered at least 90 days before the increase takes effect. Where any other statute, regulation, recorded regulatory agreement or contract requires a longer notice period, that longer period applies.
notes: CA: Civ. Code s827, primary text supplied by Taylor 2026-09-19 (amended by SB 1103, Stats. 2024 ch. 1015, eff. 2025-01-01). Sits in DIVISION 2 (Property), Title 3 - a third code location for CA landlord-tenant law after Chapter 2 and Chapter 4. CRITICAL INTERACTION: this notice rule is INDEPENDENT of s1947.12 and applies even to units EXEMPT from the Tenant Protection Act. A landlord on an exempt single-family home has no rent cap but still owes 30 or 90 days' notice. Do not condition this row on TPA coverage. The 10 percent threshold is CUMULATIVE over the 12 months before the effective date, measured against the rent charged at any time in that window - so two 6 percent increases in a year push the second into the 90-day tier. s827(b)(3)(B) carves out increases caused by a change in income or family composition determined by a statutory or regulatory recertification: those revert to 30 days. SERVICE: personal delivery or mail under CCP s1013, READ 2026-09-19. The extension is FIVE CALENDAR DAYS where address and mailing place are both in California, 10 days if either is outside CA but within the US, 12 days for a Secretary of State address-confidentiality-program address, and 20 days if either is outside the US. A mailed increase within CA is therefore effectively 35 days at the 10-percent-or-less tier and 95 days above it, and the app must compute from the service method, not the tier alone. CCP s1013(c): two COURT days for Express Mail or overnight; s1013(e): two court days for fax, only where both parties agreed in writing; s1013(g) routes electronic service to CCP s1010.6 and the Rules of Court, NOT READ. s827(a) governs changing OTHER lease terms (30 days for month-to-month), and permits the parties to agree in writing that a terms-change notice may be given not less than seven days before expiration of a term - an opt-in landlord right of the s1946.2(b)(2)(A)(ii) family, not yet drafted as a row. s827(a)(2): a served notice itself establishes the new terms as part of the lease if the tenant holds over. Commercial/qualified-commercial-tenant limbs at s827(b)(1),(4)-(7) are out of scope. GROUP NORMALISED 2026-09-19: 'Rent & Fees' -> 'Rent & Payment' (session drift; 12 canonical groups are used by all nine states).

title: Tenant Care of Premises
bodyText: Tenant shall keep the part of the premises Tenant occupies and uses clean and sanitary as the condition of the premises permits; dispose of all rubbish, garbage and other waste from the dwelling unit in a clean and sanitary manner; properly use and operate all electrical, gas and plumbing fixtures and keep them as clean and sanitary as their condition permits; neither do, nor permit any person on the premises with Tenant's permission to do, anything that willfully or wantonly destroys, defaces, damages, impairs or removes any part of the structure or dwelling unit or its facilities, equipment or appurtenances; and use the premises as Tenant's abode, using portions of it for living, sleeping, cooking or dining only as those portions were designed or intended to be used. Tenant shall repair deteriorations or injuries to the premises caused by Tenant's want of ordinary care.
notes: CA: Civ. Code ss1941.2 and 1929, primary text supplied by Taylor 2026-09-19. These are the two provisions cross-referenced by s1942(c) as disqualifying a tenant from repair-and-deduct, so they are the other half of repair-and-deduct-ca. s1941.2(a) is NOT a free-standing tenant duty clause - it is a CONDITION ON THE LANDLORD'S DUTY: the landlord's s1941/s1942 repair obligation does not arise where the tenant is in SUBSTANTIAL violation AND the violation CONTRIBUTES SUBSTANTIALLY to the dilapidation or substantially interferes with the landlord's ability to repair. Both qualifiers matter; a clause that recites the five duties without them overstates the landlord's position. rule_type RECOMMENDED rather than REQUIRED for that reason - the statute does not require these terms in a lease, it defines when the landlord is excused. TRAP AT s1941.2(b): paragraphs (a)(1) and (a)(2) - cleanliness and waste disposal - DO NOT APPLY where the landlord has EXPRESSLY AGREED IN WRITING to perform them. So a lease in which the landlord undertakes cleaning or waste removal silently disables those two limbs as an excuse. Screen any CA lease that bundles janitorial or trash service. s1929 is the general hiring rule (want of ordinary care) and sits in Chapter 1, not Chapter 2. SUPERSEDES tenant-maintenance for CA as of 2026-09-19: the overlap check found both rows stating the same tenant care duties, which would have put them in a CA lease twice. This row tracks s1941.2 and governs.

title: Application screening fees
bodyText: A landlord may charge an application screening fee only to cover the actual cost of screening, capped at a statutory amount that is adjusted annually for inflation, and may not charge one at all when the landlord knows or should know that no unit is or will soon be available. The landlord must also operate one of two processes: either consider completed applications in the order received against written screening criteria given to the applicant with the application form and approve the first applicant who meets them, or return the entire fee to every applicant not selected within seven days of selecting a tenant or thirty days of the application, whichever comes first. The landlord must give the applicant an itemized receipt, refund any part of the fee not actually used, and give the applicant a copy of any consumer credit report obtained within seven days of receiving it.
notes: CA: Civ. Code s1950.6, primary text supplied by Taylor 2026-09-19. AMENDED BY AB 1170, Stats. 2025 ch. 67, EFFECTIVE 2026-01-01 - one of the most recently changed provisions in the CA set, and squarely in the legal-watch zone. DO NOT HARDCODE $30. s1950.6(b) caps the fee at the lesser of actual out-of-pocket cost plus the reasonable value of time spent, or $30 per applicant, BUT the $30 'may be adjusted annually by the landlord or their agent commensurate with an increase in the Consumer Price Index, beginning on January 1, 1998'. The operative figure today is therefore a CPI-indexed number well above $30, computed from a 1998 base, and it is landlord-computed rather than published. Body text deliberately says 'a statutory amount adjusted annually for inflation' rather than stating a number. The app should not assert a figure it cannot derive. s1950.6(c)(2) is the structural obligation and it is new to this project: the landlord must OFFER one of two defined processes - (A) first-come-first-considered against written criteria supplied WITH THE APPLICATION FORM, first qualifying applicant approved, no fee until the application is actually considered, with a 7-day refund for inadvertent duplicate collection (or, at the applicant's option, transfer to another unit); or (B) full refund to every non-selected applicant within 7 days of selection or 30 days of application, whichever is first. This is product workflow, not lease text. s1950.6(c)(1): no fee where the landlord knows or should know no unit is or will soon be available. s1950.6(d) itemized receipt; (e) refund of the unused portion where no reference check or credit report was obtained; (f) copy of the consumer credit report to the applicant within 7 days of receipt. s1950.6(k): the fee is NOT 'security' under s1950.5 and not an 'advance fee' - so it sits outside the AB 12 deposit cap entirely. s1950.6(j) includes GUARANTORS AND COSIGNERS in 'applicant'. s1950.1 READ 2026-09-19 - see edu-reusable-screening-report-ca. The interaction matters: s1950.1(d) applies 'notwithstanding Section 1950.6', so a landlord who elects to accept reusable reports may charge an applicant who supplies one NEITHER an access fee NOR an application screening fee at all.

title: Three-day notice content and service
bodyText: California's three-day notices are governed by statute rather than by the lease. The three days exclude Saturdays, Sundays and judicial holidays. A notice demanding rent must state the amount due and the name, telephone number and address of the person to whom rent is to be paid, with the usual days and hours that person is available if payment may be made personally; alternatively it may give a financial institution account number with the institution's name and street address, provided the institution is within five miles of the rental property, or refer to an electronic funds transfer procedure already established. It must be served on the tenant and on any subtenant in actual occupation, and may be served at any time within one year after the rent becomes due. A notice to perform other covenants gives the tenant, a subtenant, a mortgagee or another interested person three days to perform and save the lease from forfeiture, and no such notice is required where the violated covenant can no longer be performed. Assigning or subletting contrary to the lease, committing waste, maintaining a nuisance or using the premises for an unlawful purpose terminates the lease and supports a three-day notice to quit with no opportunity to cure. Notices may be served by personal delivery; by leaving a copy with a person of suitable age and discretion at the tenant's residence or usual place of business and mailing a copy to the residence; or, where neither can be ascertained and no suitable person is found, by posting conspicuously on the property, delivering to a person residing there if one can be found, and mailing to the property. A landlord may not charge any fee for serving, posting or delivering these notices.
notes: CA: CCP ss1161 and 1162, primary text supplied by Taylor 2026-09-19. s1161 amended by SB 611 (Stats. 2024 ch. 287), OPERATIVE 2025-02-01. Routed to LANDLORD_EDUCATION per the standing decision to send notice-and-cure mechanics to the legal tracker rather than into lease text. The s1161(2) content list MIRRORS Civ. Code s1962 almost exactly, INCLUDING THE FIVE-MILE FINANCIAL-INSTITUTION LIMIT and the conclusive-presumption-on-mailing proviso. The two must stay consistent: the lease disclosure under owner-identity-disclosure-ca supplies the same facts the pay-or-quit notice must recite, and s1962(c) separately bars a non-compliant SUCCESSOR owner from serving a s1161(2) notice for rent accrued during noncompliance. Getting the lease disclosure wrong therefore breaks the eviction notice too. The three days EXCLUDE Saturdays, Sundays and judicial holidays, in both s1161(2) and the s1161(3) cure window. A one-year outer limit applies to serving a rent notice. s1161(3): the cure right runs to the tenant, a subtenant in actual occupation, a MORTGAGEE OF THE TERM, or another person interested in its continuance - broader than the tenant alone. No notice is required where the violated covenant cannot afterward be performed. s1161(4): assignment or subletting contrary to the lease, waste, nuisance or unlawful purpose TERMINATES the lease by operation of the statute and supports a three-day notice to quit with NO cure right. Cross-references Civ. Code ss3482.8, 3485(c) and 3486(c), ALL READ 2026-09-19 - see edu-nuisance-eviction-assignment-ca. Only s3482.8 (dogfighting/cockfighting) is statewide. s3486 applies ONLY in the City of Los Angeles. s3485 APPEARS TO BE REPEALED as of 2024-01-01 by its own s3485(j), which means s1161(4) carries a cross-reference to a section that no longer exists - and s1161 was itself amended by SB 611 in 2024 and made operative 2025-02-01 without fixing it. Do not treat the s1161(4) deemed-nuisance list as three live statewide grounds; as read, it is one statewide ground, one city-specific ground, and one dead pointer. s1161(7): 'tenant' excludes occupancies described in Civ. Code s1940(b), READ 2026-09-19 - see edu-tenancy-scope-ca. Two exclusions: transient occupancy subject to transient occupancy tax under R&T s7280, and hotel/motel occupancy where the innkeeper retains a right of access AND all five listed services are offered. Anyone outside those exclusions is a 'tenant' for s1161 purposes. s1162(a) gives the three residential service methods; s1162(b)-(c) are commercial and out of scope. Note s1946.1(f) permits certified or registered mail as an ALTERNATIVE to s1162 service for a periodic-tenancy termination, whereas s1162 does not list mail alone as a method - the two regimes differ and must not be merged in the tracker. INTERACTION NOT RESOLVED: s1946.2(c) requires a cure opportunity 'pursuant to paragraph (3) of Section 1161' before a just-cause termination for a curable breach; how that sequences against a s1161(4) no-cure ground has not been worked through.

title: Who counts as a tenant, and which occupancies fall outside the chapter
bodyText: California's residential landlord-tenant chapter applies to everyone who hires a dwelling unit in the state, including tenants, lessees, boarders and lodgers, however they are described in the agreement. A dwelling unit means a structure or part of a structure used as a home, residence or sleeping place by one person maintaining a household or by two or more people maintaining a common household. Two occupancies are outside the chapter: transient occupancy in a hotel, motel, residence club or similar facility where the stay is subject to transient occupancy tax, and occupancy at a hotel or motel where the innkeeper keeps a right of access to and control of the unit and the establishment offers all of five services to every resident - personal property safekeeping, central telephone service under filed tariffs, maid, mail and room services, occupancy for periods of less than seven days, and food service from an establishment on or next to the premises connected to the innkeeper. Unless a particular provision says otherwise by its own terms, the chapter's provisions apply to a tenancy in a dwelling unit.
notes: CA: Civ. Code s1940, read section-open 2026-09-19, together with s1961 for the separate Chapter 4 disclosure scope. Matters for a property-management product because it decides whether the whole CA clause set applies at all. s1940(a) reaches 'boarders, lodgers, and others, HOWEVER DENOMINATED', so calling an agreement a licence, a room-share or a lodging arrangement does not move it out of the chapter. s1940(b)(2): the hotel/motel exclusion is CONJUNCTIVE - the innkeeper must retain a right of access AND ALL FIVE services must be offered to all residents. A short-stay operator missing any one of the five is inside the chapter and owes the full CA clause set. This is the provision a short-term-rental operator is most likely to assume protects them. s1940(d) is a construction rule worth keeping: nothing limits the application of any Chapter 2 provision to a tenancy in a dwelling unit UNLESS the provision is so limited by its specific terms - i.e. read the chapter broadly by default. READING FLAGGED, NOT ASSERTED: s1940(b)(1) contains a double negative - the transient exclusion does not apply to 'a person to whom this paragraph pertains if the person has not made valid payment for all room and other related charges owing as of the last day on which his or her occupancy is or would be subject to tax'. On its face that keeps a non-paying transient OUTSIDE the chapter, but the sentence is genuinely awkward and the practical question - when a hotel guest who overstays becomes a tenant entitled to unlawful-detainer process - is the kind of thing that turns on case law. NOT researched. Do not build occupancy-type logic on this subdivision without confirming it. s1940(c)'s 'dwelling unit' definition is also the hinge for CCP s1162(c)'s commercial-tenant carve-out, so the two travel together. R&T s7280 READ 2026-09-19 and it supplies the operative line: s7280(a) authorises the tax on occupancy of a hotel, inn, tourist home, motel or other lodging 'UNLESS THE OCCUPANCY IS FOR A PERIOD OF MORE THAN 30 DAYS'. Because s1940(b)(1) excludes occupancy that IS OR WOULD BE subject to that tax, the 30-day line governs even in a jurisdiction that never levied one. So a stay of MORE THAN 30 DAYS is outside the transient exclusion and inside Chapter 2, subject still to the separate s1940(b)(2) five-service hotel exclusion. That is the concrete boundary a short-stay operator needs. s7280(c) also sweeps campground and RV-park spaces into 'other lodging', while excluding local-government facilities, time-share owner occupancy and s7282 campsites. The s1940(b)(1) non-payment double negative flagged above is a SEPARATE question and is still unresolved. EXCEPTION ADDED 2026-09-19: Civ. Code s1940.1 bars requiring a residential hotel occupant to move or check out and re-register before 30 days for the purpose of preserving transient status, with a rebuttable presumption of that purpose from any required check-out ($500 civil penalty). And Civ. Code s1954.071 moves the line from 30 days to 270 for DISASTER-DISPLACED guests until 2031-01-01 - see edu-disaster-displaced-guests-ca.

title: Reusable tenant screening reports
bodyText: California lets a rental applicant supply a reusable tenant screening report - a consumer report prepared within the previous 30 days at the applicant's own request and expense, made available to the landlord at no cost either directly or through a third-party service. Such a report must include the applicant's name and contact information, verification of employment, last known address, and the results of an eviction history check, and must state prominently the date through which its information is current. A landlord is not required to accept these reports. A landlord who does accept them may ask the applicant to confirm that nothing in the report has materially changed, but may not charge that applicant any fee to access the report and may not charge an application screening fee at all. Where a local ordinance conflicts with these rules, whichever gives applicants greater protection applies.
notes: CA: Civ. Code s1950.1, primary text supplied by Taylor 2026-09-19 (added by AB 2559, Stats. 2022 ch. 288, eff. 2023-01-01). Closes the s1950.6(g) dependency. THE DECISION POINT IS BINARY AND HAS A PRICE: s1950.1(h) says a landlord need not accept reusable reports, but s1950.1(d) provides that IF the landlord accepts them and an applicant supplies one, the landlord may charge NEITHER an access fee NOR an application screening fee - 'notwithstanding Section 1950.6'. So electing to accept them forfeits screening-fee revenue from every applicant who brings one. The app should surface this as a landlord-level setting, not a per-application choice. s1950.1(e)(6): the report must have been prepared WITHIN THE PREVIOUS 30 DAYS, at the applicant's request AND EXPENSE, and be available to the landlord AT NO COST - a report the landlord must pay to access is not a reusable screening report and does not trigger the fee ban. s1950.1(g) is a one-way local-preemption rule: where a local policy conflicts, whichever gives APPLICANTS GREATER PROTECTION applies. Third CA provision found deferring to the municipal layer, after s1946.2(i) and s1947.12(d)(3), and it reinforces edu-municipal-layer-ca. UNREAD AREA SURFACED BY s1950.1(f): criminal-history consideration in housing is governed by 2 CCR Art. 24, s12264 et seq. (Civil Rights Council again) plus local ordinances. That is an entire tenant-screening regulatory area this pass has NOT touched and it is not in the canvass. Flagging it as a gap-discovery find, not resolving it.

title: Nuisance-based eviction and the city-prosecutor assignment
bodyText: California deems certain conduct a nuisance for the purpose of a three-day notice to quit, but the provisions are narrower than they appear. Using a building or property for dogfighting or cockfighting is a public nuisance statewide. A separate controlled-substance eviction procedure lets a city prosecutor or city attorney bring an unlawful detainer action, but it operates only in the City of Los Angeles. Under that procedure the prosecutor must first give the owner 30 calendar days' written notice requiring the owner to act, and the owner must within 30 days either supply all relevant information or give a written safety-related explanation together with an assignment of the right to bring the action. Accepting the assignment can cost the owner up to $600 in investigation, discovery and attorney's fees. If the owner does not act, or does not prosecute the action diligently and in good faith, the prosecutor may file and join the owner as a defendant, and on a finding of unlawful detainer the prosecutor's costs may be assessed against the owner and recorded as a lien on the property. The court may order a partial eviction removing only the person involved and barring their return, rather than ending the whole tenancy.
notes: CA: Civ. Code ss3482.8, 3485 and 3486, primary text supplied by Taylor 2026-09-19. These are the three sections CCP s1161(4) incorporates as deemed nuisances. Reading them changes what that limb is worth. s3482.8 (added SB 426, eff. 2012-01-01): dogfighting under Pen. Code s597.5 or cockfighting under s597b(b) - STATEWIDE, and the only one of the three that is. s3486: controlled-substance purpose, defined at s3486(c) by a long list of H&S Code offences. s3486(g): 'This section applies ONLY IN THE COUNTY OF LOS ANGELES to a court having jurisdiction over unlawful detainer cases involving real property situated in the CITY OF LOS ANGELES.' s3486(h) further conditioned its 2014 operativity on the City of LA's reporting compliance. s3485 (unlawful weapons or ammunition): APPEARS REPEALED. s3485(j) reads 'This section shall remain in effect only until January 1, 2024, and as of that date is repealed', and the codifier's annotation says 'Repealed as of January 1, 2024, by its own provisions.' Corroborating but not conclusive: the text supplied is served as the 2022 California Code while ss3482.8 and 3486 came as 2025, which is what a publisher does when a section has left the current code. Same evidentiary posture as s2924.85 - strong, one notch below CITED. CONFIRM against the current Civil Code index at sync. SECOND INSTANCE OF CROSS-REFERENCE ROT IN CA, and worse than the 2 CCR s12178(f) case: there the target existed but had been re-lettered; here the target is GONE, and CCP s1161(4) was amended by SB 611 in 2024 and made operative 2025-02-01 while still citing it. LANDLORD EXPOSURE is the reason this is an education row rather than a footnote: s3486(a)(1)(E) puts up to $600 of the prosecutor's costs on the owner upon acceptance of an assignment, and s3486(a)(3) assesses the prosecutor's costs against the DEFENDANT OWNER with an abstract of judgment becoming A LIEN ON THE PROPERTY. An owner who ignores a 30-day notice can be joined as a defendant in an action against their own tenant. s3486(b) partial eviction: the court may remove and permanently bar an individual, including a household member, without terminating the tenancy, and may condition the remaining tenancy on the others not inviting that person back. s3486(f)(2)(B) gives the tenant an extreme-hardship stay on clear and convincing evidence, expressly NOT available on economic hardship alone. s3486(a)(5) preserves CCP s1179 relief from forfeiture - NOT READ. TYPE SIZE AND TRANSLATION AGAIN: s3486(a)(1)(C) requires the tenant notice in at least 14-POINT BOLD TYPE and in English plus all the s1632 languages. Fifth type-size floor found in CA and a third s1632 linkage - though this notice is the prosecutor's to serve, not the landlord's, so it is not lease content. s3485 EVIDENCE UPGRADED 2026-09-19, WITH A CAVEAT THE s2924.85 REPEAL DOES NOT CARRY: AB 2930 (Stats. 2018 ch. 880) as enacted on leginfo sunsets s3485 on 2024-01-01; the federal OJP National Gang Center legislation index, citing LexisNexis, lists it 'Repealed effective January 1, 2024'; Justia's latest version is 2022. BUT s3485 HAS BEEN REPEALED AND REVIVED BEFORE - AB 1013 (2007), AB 530 (2009), AB 2310 (2014, re-adding it after a lapse) and AB 2930 (2018). The 2014 revival came AFTER a lapse, so a post-2024 revival is plausible on the section's own history. Two targeted searches found every prior revival and NONE after 2018; per the two-attempt rule the search stopped there. Treat as repealed, but this is the one row in the CA set where a legal-watch hit is genuinely likely: watch for any bill adding s3485 to the Civil Code. FULL s3485 TEXT READ 2026-09-19 (2022 version, the last published): s3485(j) confirms the 2024-01-01 sunset from the section's own words, not just the enacting bill. SCOPE WHILE IN FORCE, s3485(f): only courts with unlawful detainer jurisdiction over property in the CITIES OF LOS ANGELES, LONG BEACH, SACRAMENTO AND OAKLAND - four cities, against s3486's one. So the named-locality pattern is stronger than recorded: both sibling sections were city-confined, to different city lists. While operative it also required a tenant notice in at least 14-POINT BOLD type, translated into every s1632(b) language, and conditioned the prosecutor's standing on annual reporting to the California Research Bureau (s3485(g)-(i)). This text does NOT resolve the revival caveat: a 2022 version shows what was repealed, not whether anything was re-added after 2024. The legal-watch item stands. REVIVAL CAVEAT NARROWED 2026-09-19: Justia's code pages are published by code year, and the s3485 page Taylor supplied is headed '2022 California Code' while every current section in this pass is headed '2025 California Code'. A section re-added by any 2023-2025 enactment would carry a later-year page. So no revival through the 2025 code year; only the CURRENT (2026) legislative session remains unchecked. Treated as repealed.

title: Permitted Payment Methods
bodyText: Landlord will allow Tenant to pay rent and the security deposit by at least one form of payment that is neither cash nor electronic funds transfer, and will allow Tenant to pay rent through a third party who provides a signed acknowledgment that they are not a tenant of the premises and that acceptance of the payment does not create a new tenancy. Landlord will not charge Tenant any fee for paying rent or the security deposit by check. If Tenant attempts to pay with a check drawn on insufficient funds or instructs the drawee to stop payment, Landlord may require cash as the exclusive form of payment for a period of up to three months, but only after giving Tenant written notice that the instrument was dishonored, stating the length of the cash-only period, and attaching a copy of the dishonored instrument.
notes: CA: Civ. Code s1947.3, primary text supplied by Taylor 2026-09-19 (amended by SB 611, Stats. 2024 ch. 287, eff. 2025-01-01). Blocks two base rows - see the CA extend manifest. s1947.3(a)(1): at least one form of payment that is NEITHER CASH NOR ELECTRONIC FUNDS TRANSFER must be allowed, so an electronic-only or cash-only rent policy is unlawful from the outset. s1947.3(d) defines EFT broadly enough to catch ACH, card, telephone and recurring transfers, and even 'transfers initiated electronically that deliver a paper instrument'. s1947.3(a)(2): cash-exclusive is permitted ONLY after a dishonored check or a stop-payment instruction, ONLY for up to THREE MONTHS, and only with a written notice that states the dishonour, states the period, and ATTACHES A COPY of the instrument - and it must comply with s827 if it changes the lease terms. s1947.3(a)(3): third-party rent payment must be allowed, subject to a signed acknowledgment; the statute supplies a substantially-prescribed form, and failure to supply it voids the landlord's obligation to accept. s1947.3(a)(3)(E) preserves the landlord's freedom not to enter a Section 8 contract. s1947.3(b): NO FEE for payment by check, for rent or security deposit. Distinct from the s1719 returned-instrument service charge - do not conflate. s1947.3(f): waiver void. SUPERSEDES acceptable-payment-methods (link set 2026-09-19; the manifest recorded the replacement but the field was never populated - the only broken link of the 19 base-to-CA replacements).

title: Political Signs
bodyText: Tenant may post or display political signs relating to an election or legislative vote, the initiative, referendum or recall process, or issues before a public commission, board or elected local body. In a multifamily dwelling such signs may be posted in the window or on the door of the premises; in a single-family dwelling they may also be posted from the yard, window, door, balcony or outside wall. Landlord may prohibit a political sign only if it is more than six square feet in size, if posting it would violate a local, state or federal law, or if it would violate a lawful provision of a common interest development governing document. Tenant will post and remove political signs within the time limits set by any local ordinance, or otherwise within the period Landlord reasonably establishes, which will begin at least 90 days before the election or vote and end at least 15 days after it.
notes: CA: Civ. Code s1940.4, primary text supplied by Taylor 2026-09-19 (added SB 337, eff. 2012-01-01). CONFIRMS the suspicion raised on the extend screen's eyeball pass: the base row common-area-use bars 'any sign, banner, or advertisement visible from outside the property without Landlord's consent', which s1940.4(a) makes unlawful as applied to political signs. common-area-use is BLOCKED for CA. The permitted display locations differ by dwelling type - window or door only in multifamily, but also yard, balcony and outside wall for a single-family dwelling - so the builder needs the property type to render this correctly. Only three grounds for prohibition, and size is a hard number: SIX SQUARE FEET. s1940.4(d) makes the TENANT solely responsible for any local-ordinance violation. s1940.4(e): a change of terms made to implement this section, noticed under s827, is NOT a diminution in housing services - which matters under a local just-cause ordinance. s1353.6, cross-referenced at s1940.4(c)(3), NOT READ.

title: Waterbeds and Liquid-Filled Bedding
bodyText: If the structure received its valid certificate of occupancy after January 1, 1973, Landlord will not refuse to rent to Tenant, or refuse to continue renting to Tenant, solely because Tenant has a waterbed or other liquid-filled bedding, provided Tenant meets the requirements of Civil Code section 1940.5. Those include furnishing Landlord, before installation, a waterbed insurance policy for property damage of at least $100,000 written by a carrier licensed in California and maintained until the bedding is removed; conforming to the floor load capacity and distributing the weight on a pedestal or frame substantially the dimensions of the mattress; installing, maintaining and removing the bedding per manufacturer, retailer or state standards, whichever is safest; and giving Landlord 24 hours' written notice before installing, removing or moving it. Landlord may inspect the installation on notice under Civil Code section 1954, may increase the security deposit by one-half of one month's rent, and may charge a reasonable administration fee.
notes: CA: Civ. Code s1940.5, primary text supplied by Taylor 2026-09-19. CONFIRMS the second suspicion from the extend screen's eyeball pass: common-area-use bans waterbeds outright, which s1940.5 forbids for any structure whose valid certificate of occupancy issued AFTER 1973-01-01. common-area-use is BLOCKED for CA on this ground as well as the political-sign ground. s1940.5(g) is a DEPOSIT-CAP EXCEPTION and is cross-noted at security-deposit-cap-ca: 'notwithstanding Section 1950.5' the owner may increase the deposit by one-half of one month's rent, plus a reasonable administration fee. A third exception to the AB 12 cap. s1940.5(f): the inspection right is expressly SUBJECT TO s1954 NOTICE, and non-conforming installation gets a three-day notice to conform or remove unless there is immediate danger to the structure. The insurance limb cross-references s1962 and s1962.5 for application content; s1962.5 NOT READ. Pre-1973 structures are outside the section entirely, so a ban there is unaffected - the builder needs the certificate-of-occupancy date, which the app does not currently capture.

title: Holdover
bodyText: If Tenant does not vacate the property by the end of the Term, Landlord may pursue any remedy allowed by law to recover possession and may recover the actual damages caused by Tenant's continued possession, including the reasonable rental value of the property for the period Tenant remains. Alternatively, Landlord may accept Tenant's continued payment of Rent, in which case this Lease will continue on a month-to-month basis on the same terms, terminable only as provided by law.
notes: CA: written 2026-09-19 to replace the base holdover row for California. CCP s1174 read section-open. CALIFORNIA SUPPLIES NO HOLDOVER MULTIPLIER, so the base row's 'holdover damages in the maximum amount permitted by applicable law for each day' resolves to NOTHING in CA - the same empty-referent defect that forced holdover-oh and holdover-sd. s1174(b) awards ACTUAL damages including rent found due, plus STATUTORY DAMAGES OF UP TO $600 only where MALICE IS SHOWN. That $600 is a court-awarded figure on a malice finding, NOT a per-day amount a lease can stipulate, and it must not be drafted as one. A stipulated per-day holdover charge would itself be liquidated damages under s1671(d) and void absent the impracticability showing, so California is doubly constrained here: no statute to point at, and a stated figure faces s1671(d). Body text therefore claims actual damages and reasonable rental value only. The month-to-month limb is deliberately 'terminable only as provided by law' rather than 'on written notice', because s1946.1 and s1946.2 both govern once the tenancy converts. s1951.5 RESOLVED 2026-09-19 (primary text supplied): it reads in its entirety 'Section 1671, relating to liquidated damages, applies to a lease of real property.' CONFIRMATORY, NOT CORRECTIVE, as predicted - s1671(c)(2) already reached a lease of real property for use as a dwelling on its own terms, and s1951.5 removes any argument that s1671 is confined to contracts for goods and services. No change to this row's analysis; the earlier flag is cleared. MALICIOUS HOLDOVER, added 2026-09-19: CCP s1174(b) - where the defendant is found guilty of unlawful detainer and MALICE is shown, the landlord may be awarded STATUTORY DAMAGES UP TO $600 in addition to actual damages including rent found due. The trier of fact decides which. A landlord remedy, not lease text. | NV: Read in full 2026-09-24 against NRS 118A (revisor text Rev. 4/15/2026, 2025 session incorporated). Applies as written: tracks NRS 118A.470 (actual damages; landlord-consented holdover is month to month on the same terms). Chosen over base holdover, whose "maximum amount permitted by law" figure has no located NV referent - the empty-referent defect this row was written to cure in CA. PROVISIONAL pending NRS Ch. 40 (any holdover multiplier there would add to, not contradict, this text). | NV (text batch 2, 2026-09-24): PROVISIONAL CLEARED. NRS 40.250: a fixed term ends without notice. NRS 40.360(2): in an unlawful-detainer judgment the court awards rent plus THREE TIMES the damages assessed. As in CA, that is a court-awarded measure, not a per-day figure a lease can stipulate; the clause's "any remedy allowed by law" preserves it.

title: Forfeiture election and the five-day redemption window
bodyText: In California a judgment in an unlawful detainer action declares the lease forfeited only if the three-day notice stated the landlord's election to declare a forfeiture. If the notice did not say so, the lease is not forfeited. Separately, where the action is for nonpayment of rent, the lease has not expired by its own terms and the notice did not elect forfeiture, the court may delay the writ for five days after judgment so that the tenant, a subtenant, a mortgagee or another interested party can pay the rent, damages and costs and be restored to the tenancy. That five-day delay is mandatory rather than discretionary where the lease is in writing, is for a term of more than one year, and contains no forfeiture clause.
notes: CA: CCP s1174(a) and (c), read section-open 2026-09-19. Routed to education because it governs notice drafting and post-judgment procedure rather than lease text. s1174(a) is a NOTICE-DRAFTING TRAP: omit the election to declare forfeiture from the s1161 notice and the lease survives the judgment. Belongs in the legal tracker's notice generator. s1174(c) IS A FOURTH INSTANCE OF THE OPT-IN PATTERN, and this time the opt-in runs the landlord's way: the five-day mandatory redemption window applies only where the written lease of more than one year 'DOES NOT CONTAIN A FORFEITURE CLAUSE'. Including a forfeiture clause removes the mandatory stay and leaves it discretionary. That is a real drafting decision the library currently does not surface, and it should be weighed against s1174(a)'s requirement that the notice elect forfeiture. NOT drafted as a clause here - flagged for Taylor's decision. s1174(e)-(m) carry an entire abandoned-personal-property regime cross-referencing Civ. Code ss1980-1991, with landlord non-liability safe harbours at (j)-(l). NONE OF THOSE SECTIONS READ - this is an unexplored area and the library has no CA abandoned-property row.

title: Rent Payment
bodyText: Tenant shall pay Landlord monthly rent of {{monthly_rent}} (Monthly Rent) in advance on the due date specified in this Lease, without demand. If the due date falls on a weekend or legal holiday, rent is due on the next business day. Nothing in this Lease limits Tenant's rights under Civil Code sections 1941 and 1942, including Tenant's right to repair and deduct the cost from rent.
notes: CA: overrides the base rent-payment row. The base text requires rent 'without demand, DEDUCTION, OR SETOFF'. Civ. Code s1942.1 makes any agreement waiving or modifying s1941 or s1942 rights VOID as contrary to public policy with respect to any condition rendering the premises untenantable, and s1942 is the repair-and-deduct remedy - so the deduction waiver is void as written. Removed rather than narrowed, and replaced with an express preservation, because a clause that is void in its most important application should not be shipped to tenants as though it bound them. 'Without demand' is retained and is unaffected. Note also that CCP s1161(2) requires a rent notice to state the amount due, which a disputed setoff complicates - see edu-three-day-notice-ca. ALSO relevant, read 2026-09-19: Civ. Code s1942.4 bars a landlord from demanding or collecting rent at all, or issuing a rent increase or a three-day pay-or-quit notice, while the four conditions in s1942.4(a) coexist. See edu-rent-demand-bar-ca.

title: Existing Condition
bodyText: Tenant has examined the property and, by signing this Lease, acknowledges its condition as of the Start Date (Existing Condition), except as otherwise noted in this Lease or in any move-in inspection record. This acknowledgment does not waive or modify Landlord's obligations under Civil Code sections 1941 and 1941.1, does not apply to any condition rendering the premises untenantable, and does not affect Tenant's rights regarding any condition that existed before the tenancy began. Landlord will deliver possession of the property to Tenant on the Start Date in the same or better condition as the Existing Condition, except for ordinary wear and tear.
notes: CA: overrides the base existing-condition row. The base text has the tenant acknowledge the property is 'in good order and repair and satisfactory condition'. Under Civ. Code s1942.1 that is void as a modification of s1941 rights to the extent it reaches any condition rendering the premises untenantable. It also works against the tenant on deposits: s1950.5(e)(2)(B) bars deducting for preexisting conditions, and a blanket good-condition recital is exactly the evidence a landlord would use to defeat that bar. Rewritten to acknowledge CONDITION rather than GOOD condition, with express carve-outs. Pairs with the s1950.5(g) move-in photograph duty at edu-deposit-photo-duty-ca, which for tenancies beginning on or after 2025-07-01 gives both parties a better record than a recital. GROUP NORMALISED 2026-09-19: 'Property Condition' -> 'Tenant Responsibilities' (session drift; 12 canonical groups are used by all nine states).

title: Services and Utilities Provided
bodyText: Landlord will provide only the services and utilities expressly specified in this Lease, and as otherwise required by applicable law. Except as to any condition that renders the premises untenantable, Landlord is not liable for an interruption or insufficiency of a service or utility resulting from causes beyond Landlord's reasonable control. Nothing in this Lease waives or modifies Landlord's obligations under Civil Code sections 1941 and 1941.1 or Tenant's rights under Civil Code section 1942.
notes: CA: overrides the base services-utilities-provided row. This is the row where I first read CA as diverging from Ohio and was wrong. The base disclaimer is limited to causes beyond the landlord's reasonable control, which Civ. Code s1953(a)(5) may not reach - but s1942.1 does: an agreement modifying s1941 or s1942 rights is void with respect to any condition rendering the premises untenantable, and water, heat and electrical service are s1941.1(a)(3)-(5) tenantability items. Ohio blocked the same row outright under s5321.13(D). CA permits the NARROWER fix rather than removal, because outside tenantability the disclaimer waives no statutory right - so the clause survives with an express tenantability carve-out. This is a genuine drafting difference between the two states on identical base text. GROUP NORMALISED 2026-09-19: 'Utilities & Services' -> 'Landlord Responsibilities' (session drift; 12 canonical groups are used by all nine states).

title: Property and Common Area Use
bodyText: Tenant will not, without Landlord's written consent, drill holes, use nails, hooks, or screws on the property, or fasten anything to its fixtures, appliances, or interior or exterior surfaces. Tenant will comply with any weight restrictions on balconies or porches and will not use them to store personal belongings without Landlord's consent. Tenant will not keep any item (such as a piano or safe) whose weight Landlord has not agreed is reasonable for the floor without Landlord's prior written consent. Tenant will not burn wax candles at the property. Except for political signs displayed as permitted by this Lease and by Civil Code section 1940.4, Tenant will not post or display any sign, banner, or advertisement visible from outside the property without Landlord's consent.
notes: CA: overrides the base common-area-use row, which carried two CA-unlawful limbs. (1) Its blanket ban on any sign visible from outside is unlawful as applied to political signs - Civ. Code s1940.4(a); carved out and cross-referenced to political-signs-ca. (2) Its flat waterbed ban is barred by s1940.5 for any structure whose valid certificate of occupancy issued after 1973-01-01; the waterbed sentence is REMOVED entirely and handled by waterbed-ca, which carries the statutory conditions. The general floor-load sentence is retained because s1940.5(b) and (d) themselves make weight and placement a condition of the waterbed right. Both limbs were caught on the extend screen's eyeball pass, not by the pattern screen. GROUP NORMALISED 2026-09-19: 'Property Use' -> 'Rules & Regulations' (session drift; 12 canonical groups are used by all nine states).

title: Pet Policy
bodyText: Tenant may keep only pets identified in writing to and approved by Landlord. Tenant will pay Landlord a pet deposit, if applicable, and pet rent of {{pet_rent_amount}} per month. Tenant is responsible for all damage, waste removal, odor, and disturbance caused by a pet. Landlord may revoke approval of a pet that becomes a nuisance or safety concern. This Section does not apply to an assistance animal, meaning a service animal or a support animal that Tenant or an occupant needs as a reasonable accommodation for a disability: no pet deposit, pet rent, additional security deposit, liability insurance or other additional fee may be charged in connection with an assistance animal, and no breed, size or weight limitation applies to one. Tenant remains responsible for the cost of repairing damage an assistance animal causes, excluding ordinary wear and tear.
notes: CA: overrides the base pet-policy row, which failed for CA on four grounds. (1) 2 CCR s12185(d)(2) bars any pet deposit, pet rent, additional security deposit, liability insurance or other fee for an assistance animal, and s12185(d)(5) bars breed, size and weight limits - carve-out added, mirroring the Ohio OAC 4112-5-07(C) fix. (2) Its indemnity limb waived future claims against the landlord contrary to Civ. Code s1953(a)(2) - REMOVED. (3) Its 'without liability to Tenant' limb was exculpatory under s1953(a)(5) - REMOVED. (4) Its right to 'enter the property and remove a pet' is not among the permitted entry purposes in Civ. Code s1954(a) - REMOVED; any entry must fit s1954 and landlord-entry-ca. Pet deposits remain subject to the s1950.5(c) cap, since a pet deposit is security however denominated. ADDITIONAL CA CONSTRAINT, read 2026-09-19: Civ. Code s1942.7 makes it unlawful to advertise in a manner designed to discourage applicants whose animal is not declawed or devocalized, to refuse or deny occupancy because of a refusal to declaw or devocalize, or to REQUIRE a tenant to declaw or devocalize any animal. 'Animal' covers any mammal, bird, reptile or amphibian - not just cats. Civil penalty up to $1,000 per advertisement or per animal, enforced by a city attorney, district attorney or other prosecutor. Screen any CA pet clause or listing for a declaw requirement.

title: Amounts Due at Signing
bodyText: Tenant will pay Landlord the following amounts, at the time specified for each: first month's Monthly Rent ({{monthly_rent}}) due at signing, and the Security Deposit ({{security_deposit}}) due at signing. The Security Deposit, together with any pet deposit or other amount taken to secure Tenant's performance, may not exceed the limit set by Civil Code section 1950.5(c). These amounts are due in addition to, and are not credited against, Rent due for any other month of the Term.
notes: CA: overrides the base due-at-signing row, whose worked example collected a PET DEPOSIT and LAST MONTH'S RENT alongside the security deposit. Civ. Code s1950.5(b) defines security as any payment to secure performance 'however denominated', so both count toward the one-month cap in s1950.5(c)(1) - the base example invites an unlawful overcollection at the moment of signing, which is also the moment s1950.5(c)(6) fixes as the operative date. Prepaid last month's rent removed from the example entirely; landlords wanting advance rent should use the s1950.5(c)(2) route (six or more months' rent on a lease of at least six months), which is a different mechanism with a different test. Exceptions to the cap that the builder must still handle: s1950.5(c)(5) two-month small-landlord exception (disapplied for service members), and s1940.5(g) half-month waterbed increase.

title: Early Termination
bodyText: Tenant may terminate this Lease before the end of the Term by giving Landlord at least 30 days' written notice. Tenant remains responsible for Rent and other obligations up to the termination date. If this Lease terminates because Tenant breaches it and abandons the property, or because Landlord terminates Tenant's right to possession for breach, Landlord may recover the damages provided by Civil Code section 1951.2. Those damages include the worth at the time of award of the amount by which the unpaid rent for the balance of the Term after the time of award exceeds the amount of the rental loss that Tenant proves could be reasonably avoided. Unpaid rent earned before termination, and rent that would have been earned between termination and the award, shall bear interest at {{judgment_interest_rate}} or, if no rate is stated, at the legal rate. Landlord may terminate this Lease early only as permitted by law, including, where this property is subject to Civil Code section 1946.2, only for a just cause stated in the notice of termination, and only after giving Tenant an opportunity to cure where the law requires one. Nothing in this Section limits any right either party has under applicable law, including Tenant's right to terminate without penalty due to active military service, or due to the property becoming uninhabitable through no fault of Tenant.
notes: CA: overrides the base early-termination row, which failed for CA on two grounds. (1) Its early termination fee - 'one month's Rent or 30% of the remaining Rent, WHICHEVER IS GREATER' - is a liquidated damages provision in a residential lease. Civ. Code s1671(c)(2) routes it to s1671(d), where it is VOID unless actual damage would have been impracticable or extremely difficult to fix, and a whichever-is-greater formula is a penalty on its face. Replaced with an actual-damages-less-mitigation measure. (2) Its landlord limb let Landlord terminate on 30 days' notice for a material breach cured within 10 days, which ignores s1946.2 just cause, the s1946.2(c) cure requirement keyed to CCP s1161(3), and the s1946.1 notice periods. Rewritten to defer to law rather than state its own timetable. The death-of-tenant clause in the base row was dropped as unverified for CA rather than carried over. Civ. Code s1951.2 (landlord's damages on abandonment and the duty to mitigate) has NOT been read and is the section that would confirm the actual-damages measure - flag before this row is relied on. UPDATED 2026-09-19 after reading Civ. Code s1951.2, which the earlier flag said was needed - and the flag was right. s1951.2(c)(1) makes the (a)(3) measure - future rent for the BALANCE OF THE TERM AFTER AWARD, less avoidable loss - available ONLY IF THE LEASE SO PROVIDES, or (c)(2) only if the lessor relet before award and proves good-faith mitigation. My first draft said 'actual damages reduced by reasonable efforts to re-rent', which tracks (a)(2) but SILENTLY FORFEITED (a)(3). The statutory recital is now in the body text. FIFTH INSTANCE of the opt-in landlord right pattern in CA, after s1946.2(b)(2)(A)(ii) owner move-in, CCP s1174(c) forfeiture clause, s827(a) seven-day terms-change notice and s1942.1's arbitration limb. s1951.2(b) adds a second drafting opportunity: interest on the (a)(1) and (a)(2) amounts runs at the rate SPECIFIED IN THE LEASE if lawful, else the legal rate - so a silent lease takes the legal rate by default. The (a)(3) amount is discounted at the FRB San Francisco discount rate plus 1 percent and is not lease-adjustable. Burden note: under (a)(2) and (a)(3) it is the LESSEE who must prove the loss could reasonably have been avoided. s1951.5 RESOLVED 2026-09-19 (primary text supplied): it reads in its entirety 'Section 1671, relating to liquidated damages, applies to a lease of real property.' CONFIRMATORY, NOT CORRECTIVE, as predicted - s1671(c)(2) already reached a lease of real property for use as a dwelling on its own terms, and s1951.5 removes any argument that s1671 is confined to contracts for goods and services. No change to this row's analysis; the earlier flag is cleared. STATE MILITARY RIGHT, added 2026-09-19: California has its own non-waivable military termination right, Mil. & Vet. Code s409 - no early-termination charge, prorated rent, advance rent refunded within 30 days. See military-lease-termination-ca. This row's preservation language already accommodates it.

title: No general right of periodic inspection
bodyText: California limits landlord entry to the purposes listed in Civil Code section 1954. A general right to conduct periodic inspections of an occupied dwelling is not among them. The only inspection the statute provides for is the initial inspection a tenant may request before the end of the tenancy under Civil Code section 1950.5(f). Entry to make necessary or agreed repairs, to supply agreed services, or to show the unit is permitted, but a lease term reserving periodic inspections has no statutory basis and any waiver of section 1954 rights is void under Civil Code section 1953(a)(1).
notes: CA: CONFIRMED ABSENT 2026-09-19 from Civ. Code s1954(a) read section-open. Exists because the base row inspection-rights grants exactly this and is BLOCKED for CA with no replacement - per the proof-of-absence standard an absence recorded only in a prose manifest is invisible to future canvasses. Caught on the extend screen's eyeball pass, not by the pattern screen. Note the practical consequence: a CA landlord wanting a mid-tenancy condition check must fit it to a s1954(a) purpose, and s1953(a)(1) means the tenant cannot agree otherwise.

title: Damages when a tenant breaches and abandons
bodyText: When a tenant breaches the lease and abandons, or the landlord ends the tenant's right to possession for breach, California lets the landlord recover unpaid rent earned before termination, the rent that would have been earned between termination and the award less whatever loss the tenant proves could reasonably have been avoided, and any other detriment proximately caused by the breach. Recovering rent for the balance of the term after the award is different: it is available only if the lease expressly provides for it, or if the landlord re-rented the property before the award and proves the re-rental was reasonable and in good faith. Interest on the pre-award amounts runs at the rate stated in the lease if lawful, otherwise at the legal rate. Making efforts to re-rent does not waive the landlord's right to damages.
notes: CA: Civ. Code s1951.2, primary text supplied by Taylor 2026-09-19. Routed to education alongside the lease clause because the mechanics are litigation measures rather than lease terms. s1951.2(c)(1) is the OPT-IN: without the recital the landlord loses the post-award balance-of-term measure entirely unless it relet before award under (c)(2) - and (c)(2) recovery is itself 'subject to any limitations specified in the lease', so a badly drafted cap can bind the landlord on that route too. s1951.2(b): interest on (a)(1) and (a)(2) at the lease rate if lawful, else the legal rate; the (a)(3) amount is discounted at the FRB San Francisco discount rate PLUS 1 PERCENT and is not lease-adjustable. s1951.2(a)(2)-(3): the burden of proving avoidable loss is on the LESSEE, which is more landlord-favourable than a general duty-to-mitigate framing suggests. s1951.2(d): mitigation efforts do not waive damages. s1951.2(e) preserves the lessor's right to INDEMNIFICATION for pre-termination personal injury or property damage liability 'where the lease provides for such indemnification' - a sixth opt-in, but it sits in tension with s1953(a)(2) (waiver of future causes of action void) depending on whether the indemnity runs to third-party liability or to the tenant's own claims. NOT RESOLVED; flag before drafting an indemnity. s1951.4, cross-referenced at s1951.2(a) as the alternative remedy that keeps the lease in effect, has NOT BEEN READ - it is reported to depend on the lease permitting assignment and subletting subject to reasonable limitations, which would be a seventh opt-in. Read it before relying on either remedy.

title: Continuation of Lease After Abandonment
bodyText: The lessor has the remedy described in California Civil Code Section 1951.4 (lessor may continue lease in effect after lessee's breach and abandonment and recover rent as it becomes due, if lessee has right to sublet or assign, subject only to reasonable limitations).
notes: CA: Civ. Code s1951.4, primary text supplied by Taylor 2026-09-19. VERBATIM SAFE-HARBOUR TEXT - s1951.4(a) states the remedy 'is available ONLY IF THE LEASE PROVIDES FOR THIS REMEDY' and then supplies this exact wording as a form that 'satisfies this subdivision'. Other wording is permitted, but there is no reason to invent any. SEVENTH CONFIRMED OPT-IN LANDLORD RIGHT IN CALIFORNIA. THIS ROW ALONE IS NOT ENOUGH, and that is the trap: s1951.4(b) makes the remedy operate only if the lease ALSO satisfies one of three sublet/assignment conditions - (1) it permits, or does not prohibit or restrict, subletting or assignment; (2) it permits them subject to express standards reasonable at execution (express standards are PRESUMED reasonable, a presumption affecting the burden of proof), with the landlord not enforcing a standard that has since become unreasonable; or (3) it permits them with landlord consent AND provides that consent shall not be unreasonably withheld, or a standard to that effect is implied by law. A lease reciting s1951.4(a) while forbidding assignment in the landlord's SOLE DISCRETION satisfies none of the three and gets nothing. See no-sublet-assign-ca. s1951.4(c): acts of maintenance or preservation, efforts to relet, appointment of a receiver at the lessor's initiative, and lawfully withholding or terminating consent to a sublet do NOT constitute terminating the lessee's right to possession - so none of them forfeits the remedy.

title: Subletting and Assignment (Reasonable Consent)
bodyText: Tenant will not sublease or assign all or any portion of the property or this Lease without Landlord's prior written consent, which Landlord will not unreasonably withhold. Tenant will not rent the property, or any portion of it, on any short-term rental or home-sharing platform.
notes: CA: overrides the base no-sublet-assign row, and this one is a JUDGMENT CALL FOR TAYLOR RATHER THAN A DEFECT FIX - the base clause is not unlawful in California, it is self-defeating. I marked no-sublet-assign 'provisionally clear' on the extend screen because a sole-discretion consent requirement is permissible in a CA residential lease. That was right as far as it went and WRONG in consequence. Civ. Code s1951.4(b) makes the continue-the-lease-and-collect-rent remedy available only if the lease (1) permits or does not restrict sublet/assignment, (2) permits it subject to express standards reasonable at execution, or (3) permits it with consent NOT UNREASONABLY WITHHELD. 'Sole discretion' satisfies none of the three, so a landlord using the base clause forfeits the s1951.4 remedy entirely - even if the lease also carries continue-lease-remedy-ca. THE TRADE-OFF, stated plainly for Taylor's decision: keep SOLE DISCRETION and retain maximum control over who occupies the property, but lose the s1951.4 remedy and be left with s1951.2 damages after termination; or adopt NOT UNREASONABLY WITHHELD, as drafted here, and keep both remedies at the cost of having to justify a refusal. Most landlords want the remedy. I have drafted the reasonableness version because s1951.4(b)(3) is the cheapest of the three routes and because s1951.4(c)(3) confirms that lawfully withholding consent does not itself forfeit the remedy - but this is reversible on request. s1951.4(b)(2) is the alternative worth considering if control matters more: express standards are PRESUMED reasonable, with the burden on the tenant. The short-term-rental sentence is carried over unchanged and is unaffected by s1951.4. CHOICE GROUP 'ca-sublet-consent' (2026-09-19): this row and no-sublet-assign-discretion-ca are ALTERNATIVES - a CA lease must contain EXACTLY ONE. This is the DEFAULT. The builder has no choice-group field yet; see the log. GROUP NORMALISED 2026-09-19: 'Property Use' -> 'Tenant Responsibilities' (session drift; 12 canonical groups are used by all nine states).

title: Termination by a Victim of Abuse or Violence
bodyText: Tenant may terminate this Lease if Tenant, a household member, or an immediate family member was the victim of domestic violence, sexual assault, stalking, human trafficking, abuse of an elder or dependent adult, a crime that caused bodily injury or death, a crime involving a firearm or other deadly weapon, or a crime involving the use or threat of force. Tenant must give Landlord written notice with one of the following attached: a copy of a qualifying restraining or protective order; a copy of a written report by a peace officer stating that a report has been filed; documentation from a qualified third party in the form set out in Civil Code section 1946.7; or any other documentation that reasonably verifies the act or crime occurred. Notice must be given within 180 days of the order, the report, or the act or crime. Tenant is responsible for rent for no more than 14 calendar days after giving notice, prorated if the property is re-rented sooner, and is released without penalty from any further obligation. Tenant will not forfeit any security deposit or advance rent because of the termination, and the termination is not a breach of this Lease. Any other tenant remains bound by this Lease.
notes: CA: Civ. Code s1946.7, primary text supplied by Taylor 2026-09-19 (SB 1017, Stats. 2022 ch. 558, eff. 2023-01-01). MUCH BROADER THAN 'DOMESTIC VIOLENCE' - s1946.7(a)(6)-(8) reach ANY crime causing bodily injury or death, any crime involving a firearm or other deadly weapon, and any crime involving force or the threat of force. A lease or a canvass row labelled 'domestic violence' understates it. s1946.7(b)(4) is a CATCH-ALL: 'any other form of documentation that reasonably verifies' the act occurred. But s1946.7(k)(2)(B) removes STATUTORY damages against the landlord where the tenant relied on (b)(4) alone - so the catch-all is easier for the tenant to use and weaker to enforce. s1946.7(f): the landlord may NOT require forfeiture of the deposit or advance rent, and the termination is not a breach for any purpose. s1946.7(g): co-tenants stay bound. s1946.7(i): the landlord MAY NOT DISCLOSE the tenant's information to third parties except on written consent or court order - a confidentiality duty. s1946.7(j): may not refuse to rent to someone who previously exercised this right. s1946.7(k): actual damages plus STATUTORY DAMAGES of $100-$5,000. s1946.7(c) is an easily-missed limb: where the victim is an immediate family member who did NOT live with the tenant and no part of the crime occurred in or within 1,000 FEET of the unit, the tenant must attach a further written statement of intent to relocate and why. CROSS-REFERENCE ERROR IN THE STATUTE'S OWN FORM, found 2026-09-19: the verbatim Qualified Third Party Statement in s1946.7(b)(3)(B) says a victim of violent crime advocate is defined 'in Section 1947.6 of the Civil Code'. s1947.6 is the ELECTRIC VEHICLE CHARGING section. The definition is actually at s1946.7(h)(5). The parallel forms in CCP s1161.3(a)(2)(C) and Civ. Code s1941.5(d)(3) both cite s1946.7 correctly, which confirms s1947.6 is a drafting slip rather than an intended cross-reference. If the app ever reproduces the s1946.7 form, reproduce it VERBATIM, error included - the statute says 'substantially the same form', and a silently 'corrected' form is no longer the statutory text - but add a builder-facing note. A third instance of cross-reference rot in CA, after 2 CCR s12185(c)(2) and CCP s1161(4).

title: Right to Summon Emergency Assistance
bodyText: Nothing in this Lease prohibits or limits Tenant, any resident, or any other person from summoning law enforcement assistance or emergency assistance on behalf of a victim of abuse, a victim of crime, or an individual in an emergency. Landlord will not impose or threaten any fee, fine, penalty, termination, non-renewal, or inferior terms of tenancy because such assistance was summoned.
notes: CA: Civ. Code s1946.8, primary text supplied by Taylor 2026-09-19 (AB 1171, eff. 2022-01-01). s1946.8(b): ANY lease provision prohibiting or limiting - or THREATENING to prohibit or limit - the right to summon assistance is VOID as contrary to public policy. s1946.8(e): waiver void. This row states the rule affirmatively rather than relying on silence, because a 'nuisance' or 'excessive police calls' clause elsewhere in a lease is the usual way the prohibition creeps in - SCREEN any CA lease for one. s1946.8(d): NO DOCUMENTATION is required to establish the person's belief that assistance was necessary. s1946.8(f)(2): REBUTTABLE PRESUMPTION that the affirmative defence is established if the landlord files an unlawful detainer WITHIN 30 DAYS of assistance being summoned and the notice alleges the summoning was a lease violation or nuisance. The landlord rebuts by showing another substantial motivating factor. 'Penalties' is defined broadly at s1946.8(a)(3) to include inferior terms and conditions of tenancy, not just fees and eviction.

title: Abuse and violence: eviction bar, lock changes, confidentiality
bodyText: A landlord may not terminate or refuse to renew a tenancy based on an act of abuse or violence against the tenant, the tenant's immediate family member, or a household member once the landlord has received qualifying documentation. There are two exceptions: where the perpetrator is a tenant in residence of the same unit, and where the perpetrator's words or actions have threatened the physical safety of other tenants, guests or invitees and the tenant continues to permit the perpetrator on the premises after a three-day notice requiring them not to. Where a person restrained by court order is a tenant of the same unit, the landlord must change the locks at the landlord's own expense within 24 hours of a written request accompanied by the order, and give the protected tenant a key; if the landlord does not, the tenant may change the locks and the landlord must reimburse the cost within 21 days. Information a tenant provides under these protections may not be disclosed to third parties without written consent or a court order. A landlord is not liable to other tenants for complying.
notes: CA: CCP s1161.3 (amended AB 1756, eff. 2024-01-01) and Civ. Code s1941.6 (amended SB 1051, eff. 2025-01-01), primary text supplied by Taylor 2026-09-19. s1161.3(b)(2)(B) is the operative landlord route and it is procedural: the three-day notice requires the TENANT not to voluntarily permit or consent to the perpetrator's presence - it is not a notice to the perpetrator, and it only works if the perpetrator's conduct threatened others' physical safety. s1161.3(c) protects the landlord from other tenants' claims arising from compliance. s1161.3(d)(2) routes same-unit-perpetrator cases to CCP s1174.27, NOT READ. s1941.6 applies ONLY where the restrained person is a TENANT OF THE SAME UNIT - a different and narrower trigger than s1161.3. The 24-hour clock runs from the written request plus the order. s1941.6(c)(3) limits the self-help lock change to leases executed on or after 2011-01-01. s1941.6(e): the excluded person remains liable for rent under the lease. s1941.6(d) disapplies s789.3 liability - s789.3 READ 2026-09-19, see edu-self-help-eviction-ban-ca. The carve-out is necessary because excluding the restrained co-tenant by a lock change would otherwise be a willful lockout within s789.3(b)(1). Confidentiality duties sit in both s1161.3(e) and Civ. Code s1946.7(i). CCP s1174.27 READ 2026-09-19 (the same-unit-perpetrator procedure s1161.3(d)(2) routes to): where the court finds documentation of abuse or violence, the defendant raising the defence and other occupants not otherwise at fault are NOT guilty and owe NOTHING - no holdover damages, costs, termination fees or attorney's fees. Where another defendant is shown to be the perpetrator and guilty, the court MUST order a PARTIAL EVICTION of that person only, WITHOUT terminating the tenancy, and MUST order the landlord to change the locks; it may bar the perpetrator permanently, taking custody and visitation arrangements into account. A s1174.27 finding is inadmissible in any other proceeding.

title: Protected classes and source-of-income rules
bodyText: California prohibits housing discrimination on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, gender, gender identity, gender expression, sexual orientation, marital status, national origin, ancestry, familial status, source of income, disability, veteran or military status, or genetic information, including a perception that a person has any of those characteristics or is associated with someone who does. Source of income includes federal, state and local public assistance and housing subsidies, expressly including Section 8 vouchers and HUD-VASH vouchers, so refusing to rent because an applicant holds a voucher is unlawful. Where there is a government rent subsidy, any financial or income standard must be based only on the portion of rent the tenant actually pays, and an applicant must be offered the option of supplying alternative evidence of ability to pay instead of a credit history. A landlord must also count the aggregate income of people residing together on the same basis as it would for married people.
notes: CA: Gov. Code ss12955 (amended SB 267, eff. 2024-01-01) and 12927 (SB 222, eff. 2020-01-01), primary text supplied by Taylor 2026-09-19. Answers two canvass rows at once. THREE OPERATIONAL RULES most likely to be breached by a screening workflow rather than by lease text: s12955(n) aggregate-income rule; s12955(o)(1)(A) subsidy income standard keyed only to the TENANT'S PORTION - a 3x-the-rent rule applied to full contract rent is unlawful for a voucher holder; and s12955(o)(1)(B) the credit-history alternative, which requires giving reasonable time AND reasonably considering the alternative evidence. These bind the app's screening logic, not the lease. s12955(b) bars INQUIRY into most protected characteristics - note source of income is deliberately absent from the (b) list and s12955(p)(2) confirms asking about level or source of income is not itself discrimination. s12927(c)(2)(A): narrow exception for renting a portion of an OWNER-OCCUPIED single-family house to ONE roomer or boarder, and even then the s12955(c) advertising ban still applies. s12927(d): 'housing accommodation' expressly includes units offered through a HOSTING PLATFORM. s12927(c)(1) is the statutory basis for the reasonable accommodation and modification duties implemented by 2 CCR ss12176-12181. ENFORCEMENT, Gov. Code ss12980-12989.3 read 2026-09-19: administrative complaint within ONE YEAR (s12980(b)); a private civil action within TWO YEARS, tolled while the complaint is pending, and available whether or not a complaint was filed (s12989.1); actual AND PUNITIVE damages, injunctions and discretionary prevailing-party fees (s12989.2); Attorney General pattern-or-practice suits with civil penalties up to $50,000 for a first violation and $100,000 for each subsequent one (s12989.3). NEW from 2026-01-01 (SB 477): s12981(a)(2) requires ALL PARTIES to take part in the department's MANDATORY DISPUTE RESOLUTION, free of charge, before the department sues. Candidate 572.7: NO RESPONDENT ELECTION RIGHT - because CA housing cases are not heard administratively at all. The department prosecutes by CIVIL ACTION in superior court (s12981(a)(1)), so there is no administrative forum for a landlord to elect out of, unlike Ohio's s4112.055(A)(2).

title: Tenant harassment and immigration-status disclosure
bodyText: California makes it unlawful for a landlord, for the purpose of influencing a tenant to vacate, to engage in conduct amounting to theft or extortion, to use or threaten force or menacing conduct interfering with the tenant's quiet enjoyment, to commit a significant and intentional violation of the entry statute, or to threaten to disclose information about the immigration or citizenship status of a tenant, occupant or anyone associated with them. A tenant who prevails may recover a civil penalty of up to $2,000 for each violation. Separately, it is unlawful to disclose such immigration or citizenship information to any immigration authority, law enforcement agency or government agency for the purpose of harassing or retaliating against a tenant, influencing them to vacate, or recovering possession. A court that finds such a disclosure must order statutory damages of between 6 and 12 times the monthly rent for each person whose status was disclosed, issue injunctive relief, and notify the district attorney.
notes: CA: Civ. Code ss1940.2 and 1940.35 (both AB 291, eff. 2018-01-01), primary text supplied by Taylor 2026-09-19. s1940.2(a)(4) is the one that connects to the rest of this state's work: a SIGNIFICANT AND INTENTIONAL VIOLATION OF s1954 is statutory harassment, so misuse of the entry right is not merely a s1954 problem - it carries the s1940.2(b) $2,000-per-violation penalty.
