Code s1668's 'violation of law' limb directly, WITHOUT any Tunkl public-interest analysis - the lower courts erred by applying Tunkl to a statutory-duty claim. Reversed and remanded. WHY THIS MATTERS MORE HERE THAN IN MOST CONTEXTS: a residential landlord's duties are overwhelmingly statutory - Civ. Code ss1941 and 1941.1, s1941.3 locks, H&S s13113.7 smoke alarms, H&S s17920.3 and s17920.10 conditions, H&S s17973 balconies, s1954 entry. After Whitehead a lease release cannot reach a claim that ANY of those was breached, irrespective of Tunkl, Henrioulle or the recreational context. LEWIS SURVIVES, BUT NARROWED: Whitehead cites Lewis Operating Corp. (2011) with apparent approval for the proposition that ordinary negligence may be released 'in certain circumstances'. So the recreational-amenity exception still exists - but only for COMMON-LAW negligence. A gym or pool release will not protect a landlord from a claim framed as a statutory or code violation, which is how most such claims can be pleaded. Practical guidance: DO NOT ship an amenity release for CA as a liability shield; at most it reaches ordinary negligence at a genuinely non-essential amenity. Two consecutive state Supreme Court decisions (Henrioulle 1978, Whitehead 2025) now point the same way, and the extend-screen exculpation blocks rest on three independent grounds: s1953(a)(5), Henrioulle, and Whitehead's s1668 statutory-duty rule.

title: Jury trial waivers in a lease are unenforceable
bodyText: In California a contractual waiver of the right to a jury trial made before any dispute arises is unenforceable unless a statute expressly authorizes it, and no statute authorizes one in a residential lease. A jury waiver clause in a California lease therefore has no effect. Separately, a residential lease provision waiving a tenant's procedural rights in litigation is void by statute.
notes: CA: CASE LAW plus statute. GRAFTON PARTNERS L.P. v. SUPERIOR COURT (2005) 36 Cal.4th 944: predispute jury trial waivers are unenforceable in California absent express statutory authorization, because CCP s631 lists the only permissible methods of waiver and none is predispute; the Court expressly overruled Trizec Properties (1991). Opinion text viewed via vLex; holding confirmed across multiple sources. A residential lease jury waiver therefore fails on TWO INDEPENDENT GROUNDS: Grafton, of general application, and Civ. Code s1953(a)(4), which voids waiver of 'procedural rights in litigation'. Either suffices. SCREEN RESULT: the extend-screen pattern search for 'jury|venue|arbitrat' across the 52 base rows found no jury waiver in the base library, so this row changes no current clause - it exists so a future clause is caught. VENUE - DELIBERATELY NOT RESOLVED: EPICENTRX, INC. v. SUPERIOR COURT (Cal. July 21, 2025, S282521) held that a forum-selection clause may be enforced against a California plaintiff even where the chosen forum offers no jury, effectively overruling Handoush v. Lease Finance Group (2019). Known here only through law-firm summaries, and it arose in a CORPORATE context. Whether it reaches a RESIDENTIAL lease - where s1953(a)(4) applies and unlawful detainer has its own statutory venue - is a separate question not researched. Do not draft a CA lease forum-selection clause on the strength of EpicentRx. VENUE RESOLVED ON THE TEXT 2026-09-19: CCP s392(a)(1) makes the superior court in the COUNTY WHERE THE PROPERTY IS SITUATED the proper court for any action to recover real property, and s392(b) fixes the unlawful detainer location to the court nearest the property. A residential lease forum-selection clause moving an eviction elsewhere would conflict with s392 and is void as a waiver of 'procedural rights in litigation' under Civ. Code s1953(a)(4). EpicentRx (Cal. 2025) concerned a corporate forum clause and the jury right; it does not displace s1953(a)(4)'s statutory bar for residential tenancies. Textual conclusion; EpicentRx itself was not read. | CA 2026-09-24 follow-up: EpicentRx, Inc. v. Superior Court (2025) 18 Cal.5th 58 (S282521) READ IN FULL; disapproves Handoush v. Lease Finance Group (2019) 41 Cal.App.5th 729. Its holding is confined to the constitutional jury right, which no statute backs with a voiding rule (art. I s16 and CCP s631 'simply state that such waivers will not be enforced'). The Court expressly preserved the line of statutes that void private waivers of rights (citing Corp. Code s31512, Civ. Code s1751, Lab. Code s219(a)); footnote 7: 'We need not and do not consider the merits of Wimsatt, America Online, Verdugo, or similar cases involving potentially unwaivable substantive rights.' Civ. Code s1953(a) is that form, so EpicentRx does not displace s1953(a)(4) for residential leases. STATED LIMIT: EpicentRx's first distinction was substantive vs procedural and s1953(a)(4) is about procedural rights, and no published case applies s1953(a)(4) to a forum-selection clause - a textual/structural conclusion, not a holding. Footnote 4 preserves overreaching/unequal-bargaining-power grounds; EpicentRx involved sophisticated parties, the opposite of an adhesion lease.

title: Accepting rent can waive a breach or renew the tenancy
bodyText: In California, a landlord who accepts rent with full knowledge of a tenant's breach waives the right to declare a forfeiture for that breach and for any earlier breach, and is estopped from relying on it. A landlord may avoid that waiver by giving the tenant notice at the time rent is accepted that acceptance is not consent to the breach or a waiver of the right to forfeit. A separate and harder rule applies after a notice terminating the tenancy has expired: accepting rent then creates a presumption that the tenancy was renewed, and a court of appeal has held that a non-waiver clause did not overcome that presumption where the tenant was not yet in breach when the rent was accepted. A non-waiver clause is more likely to hold where the landlord accepts rent after an actual breach, such as unpaid rent following a three-day notice. As a practical matter, rent tendered after a three-day or termination notice expires should be returned rather than accepted if the landlord intends to proceed.
notes: CA: CASE LAW plus Civ. Code s1945. RESOLVES the late-rent acceptance question, and it splits into TWO RULES that must not be merged. RULE 1 - WAIVER OF FORFEITURE FOR A BREACH. KERN SUNSET OIL CO. v. GOOD ROADS OIL CO. (1931, Cal. Supreme Court): accepting rent with full knowledge of a breach waives forfeiture for that breach and any earlier one. Stated in CACI No. 4324, 'Affirmative Defense - Waiver by Acceptance of Rent' - a Judicial Council jury instruction, which is an authoritative statement of the rule. KARBELNIG v. BROTHWELL (1966) 244 Cal.App.2d 333: waiver was AVOIDED where the lease had a non-waiver clause AND the landlord gave CONTEMPORANEOUS NOTICE at acceptance. A Glenn County Superior Court self-help page confirms that a landlord's post-notice waiver nullifies the forfeiture election. RULE 2 - RENEWAL AFTER A TERMINATION NOTICE EXPIRES. Civ. Code s1945 presumes renewal where the lessor accepts rent after expiration. BACA v. KUANG (Cal. Ct. App., c. 2025): a landlord who accepted rent after a 30-day termination notice expired was held to have renewed month-to-month, and the lease's HOLDOVER AND NON-WAIVER PROVISIONS DID NOT REBUT the presumption; the landlord's subjective belief was immaterial. Known ONLY through a law-firm alert (Ballard Spahr) - opinion NOT read - and it was a COMMERCIAL lease. PRODUCT CONSEQUENCE - this bears directly on the reservation-of-rights feature on the legal-tracker roadmap. In CA a contemporaneous reservation notice at acceptance is the Karbelnig route and is worth building, but Baca suggests it is NOT enough after a termination notice has expired: the safe course there is to REFUSE or RETURN the payment. So the CA version of that feature needs a second branch - 'return, don't reserve' once a notice has run. CCP s1161.1 permits a COMMERCIAL landlord to accept partial rent after notice and still proceed; secondary sources describe no residential equivalent. s1161.1 NOT READ. | CA 2026-09-24 follow-up: Baca v. Kuang (2025) 107 Cal.App.5th 1292 (1st Dist., Div. 5, No. A171071; published except Discussion parts B and E) READ IN FULL. Holds that a landlord who deposits and retains rent after a termination notice expires triggers the Civ. Code s1945 renewal presumption regardless of subjective intent; the presumption is rebuttable; filing the unlawful detainer did not rebut it; each later unqualified acceptance creates a fresh presumption. Reasoning rests on s1945's text ('a lessee of real property') and on residential authority (Kaufman v. Goldman (2011) 195 Cal.App.4th 734, where returning checks uncashed and refunding one mistakenly deposited meant no acceptance), so it reaches residential tenancies and is the direct authority for 'return, don't reserve'. CCP s1161.1's partial-rent safe harbor is commercial-only, so residential landlords have less protection. BODYTEXT CORRECTED: the prior sentence said non-waiver and holdover clauses 'did not overcome' the presumption - too broad. The clause in Baca failed because it addressed waiver of a PRECEDING BREACH and there was none (the lease's own 10-day cure period meant holding over was not yet a breach); Woodman Partners v. Sofa U Love (2001) 94 Cal.App.4th 766 shows a no-waiver clause can work after an actual breach. See also Superior Strut & Hanger Co. v. Port of Oakland (1977) 72 Cal.App.3d 987; Aviel v. Ng (2008) 161 Cal.App.4th 809.

title: No lockouts, utility shutoffs or removal of belongings
bodyText: A California landlord may not, with intent to end a residential tenancy, willfully cause any utility service to the tenant to be interrupted or terminated - including water, heat, light, electricity, gas, telephone, elevator or refrigeration - whether or not the landlord controls the utility. Nor may the landlord change the locks or use a bootlock or similar device to keep the tenant out, remove outside doors or windows, or remove the tenant's belongings or furnishings without the tenant's prior written consent, except under the statutory procedure for property left after a tenancy ends. The only lawful way to remove a tenant is through a court eviction carried out by the appropriate authorities. A landlord who violates this is liable for the tenant's actual damages plus up to $100 for each day or part of a day the violation continues, with a minimum of $250 for each separate violation, and the prevailing party recovers attorney's fees. A repeat violation on a later occasion counts as a new violation with its own award.
notes: CA: Civ. Code s789.3, primary text supplied by Taylor 2026-09-19 (amended Stats. 1979 ch. 333). CLOSES THE GAP IDENTIFIED IN s5.25: California's self-help eviction ban had no row. It sits in DIVISION 2 (Property), Part 2, Title 2, Chapter 2 'Termination of Estates' - an entirely different division from the Title 5 landlord-tenant chapters, which is why the Chapters 1-2 sweep missed it. The seventh cross-chapter confirmation in CA and the most consequential. THE INTENT ELEMENT is the key to applying it correctly: every limb requires the act be done 'with intent to terminate the occupancy' and 'willfully'. A utility outage the landlord did not cause for that purpose, or a lock change made for a lawful reason, is outside it. That is why s1941.6(d) needs to EXPRESSLY disapply s789.3 for a court-ordered DV lock change - the exclusion there would otherwise be a lockout of the restrained person. Cross-noted at edu-abuse-violence-protections-ca. s789.3(a) reaches utilities 'whether or not the utility service is under the control of the landlord' - so INDIRECTLY causing a shutoff, e.g. by not paying a landlord-account utility with intent to force the tenant out, is within it. s789.3(b)(3) property removal is lawful ONLY through the Civ. Code s1980 et seq. procedure - which ties this row directly to edu-abandoned-property-ca. Removing belongings outside that procedure is both a s789.3 violation and a loss of the s1989 liability shield. REMEDY SHAPE, s789.3(c): actual damages PLUS a DAILY penalty up to $100 with a $250 MINIMUM PER SEPARATE CAUSE OF ACTION, and non-contemporaneous repeat violations are separate causes of action with separate awards. So the exposure ACCRUES DAILY - a three-week lockout is up to $2,100 before actual damages. Compare the candidate-table figures: CO greater of 3x rent or $5,000; KS 1.5 months' rent; MN treble or $500. CA's per-violation floor is lower but its daily accrual is uncapped. s789.3(d): prevailing-party fees, injunctive relief during the action, non-exclusive. s789.3(b) final paragraph excludes the s1940(b) transient occupancies and expressly preserves lawful eviction by appropriate legal authorities. PRODUCT CONSEQUENCE: the legal tracker and any automated late-rent workflow must NEVER suggest a lock change, utility interruption, or removal of belongings as a nonpayment remedy in CA. It also bears on s1940.2(a)(3) harassment and the s1942.5 retaliation window, which can stack on the same conduct.

title: Military tenants: no chain-of-command contact, no waivers
bodyText: In collecting any debt or payment from a member of the active California militia or an active or reserve member of the Armed Forces, including unpaid rent, a California landlord may not contact the member's military unit or chain of command without the member's written consent, and that consent counts only if it is given after the obligation has become due and payable. A lease clause consenting in advance to contact with a commanding officer is therefore ineffective, and any waiver of these protections is void. A landlord may not condition a military or veteran discount on the tenant waiving any legal right. A service member's application for or receipt of a stay or postponement of an obligation under California's military protections may not by itself be treated as showing that the member cannot pay. A landlord may not electronically access a service member's Common Access Card, place it in a card reader, or ask for its PIN. Violations carry actual damages, attorney's fees and costs, and are a misdemeanor.
notes: CA: Mil. & Vet. Code s401, primary text supplied by Taylor 2026-09-19 (amended SB 1311, Stats. 2022 ch. 620, eff. 2023-01-01), read with the s400 definitions. NOT a lease-termination right - s401 is a set of debt-collection, credit and anti-waiver protections - but it bears on landlords directly. s401(c) IS THE LANDLORD-FACING RULE and the one most likely to be breached: contacting a military tenant's UNIT OR CHAIN OF COMMAND to collect rent is a common landlord tactic, and it is barred unless the member gives written consent AFTER the rent is due and payable. That timing requirement means NO LEASE CLAUSE can supply the consent - consent in a lease is necessarily given before any obligation is due - and s401(e)(2) voids any waiver of a right this code gives service members. Screen found no such clause in the current library; this row exists so one is never added. Note the protected class under (c) is broader than the s400(d) 'service member' definition: it reaches any member of the active militia or an active OR RESERVE component, regardless of active orders. s401(a)(1) applies to 'any lender OR OTHER PERSON', which reaches a landlord: use of a Chapter 7.5 stay may not by itself ground a finding of inability to pay. Relevant to screening and to s1954.07 rent reporting. s401(e)(1): a military or veteran discount may not be conditioned on waiving any right - relevant if a landlord offers military pricing. s401(d): CAC card access in a transaction voids the transaction; photocopying is not addressed by the text and was not researched. REMEDIES: s401(f) actual damages, fees and costs; s401(g) misdemeanor, up to one year and/or $1,000. s402 SINCE READ - default-judgment declaration, 120-day lookback, mandatory 90-day stay; see edu-military-default-judgment-ca. s403 (stays) also read. CHAPTER 7.5 NOW READ IN FULL (2026-09-19). CA DOES have a state lease-termination right - s409, see military-lease-termination-ca. s409.15 imposes a 30-DAY WRITTEN-RESPONSE duty on any good-faith request for relief, on pain of waiving objection. s405 caps interest at 6% on PRE-service interest-bearing obligations and defines interest to include fees and charges - an ordinary lease does not bear interest, so it will rarely reach rent, but it would reach a pre-service payment plan charging interest. Whether CA's protections as a whole are narrower or broader than the federal SCRA was not assessed - the federal statute was not read. Federal SCRA 50 U.S.C. s3955 governs termination regardless - see early-termination-ca.

title: Military tenants in eviction: declaration, stays and dependents
bodyText: Before a California court will enter a default judgment - which is how most eviction cases end - the landlord must file a declaration under penalty of perjury stating facts showing the tenant is not in military service, or else declaring that the tenant is in service or that the landlord cannot determine whether they are. A tenant counts as in military service if they are currently serving or served within the preceding 120 days. Without a declaration showing the tenant is not in service, judgment cannot be entered without a court order, and if the tenant is in service the court must first appoint an attorney to represent them; the court may also require the landlord to post a bond. Where a defense may exist that cannot be presented without the tenant, the court must stay the case for at least 90 days. A judgment entered against a service member during service or within 30 days after may be reopened on application within 90 days after service ends. Knowingly making a false declaration is a misdemeanor, and carries liability for damages and attorney's fees. Separately, at any stage of any case involving a service member during service or within 120 days after, the court must stay the case on the service member's application unless their military service does not materially affect their ability to take part, and on the same test may stay execution of any judgment - including an eviction order - and vacate or stay any attachment or garnishment. A stay can run for the period of service plus three months, on terms the court sets, which may include payment in installments. No fine or penalty accrues during a stay of an action to enforce a contract, and a court may relieve a service member from a penalty - such as a late fee - incurred while in service if service materially impaired their ability to pay. Where the service member is one of several co-tenants, the landlord may, with the court's leave, proceed against the others. Where the unit is occupied primarily as a home by a service member's spouse, children or other dependents, no eviction may be carried out during the period of military service or until 120 days after release except with the court's permission, and the court must stay the case or order partial payments on application unless the tenant's ability to pay is unaffected. Knowingly taking part in such an eviction is a misdemeanor.
notes: CA: Mil. & Vet. Code s402, primary text supplied by Taylor 2026-09-19 (amended SB 1097, Stats. 2024 ch. 129, eff. 2025-01-01). The state analog of the federal SCRA default-judgment protections, applying in ANY action - and therefore to every unlawful detainer. A LEGAL-TRACKER STEP, not lease text: the eviction workflow must prompt for this declaration before any default judgment is requested. s402(f) IS THE DETAIL TO BUILD AROUND: 'in the military service' includes anyone who SERVED WITHIN THE PRECEDING 120 DAYS, not only those currently serving. A status check run only against current service is therefore insufficient in CA. 'Military service' itself is the s400(c) definition - militia on full-time active state or federal service, or otherwise full-time active duty exceeding seven days in any 14-day period. s402(a): three possible declarations - NOT in service; IN service; or UNABLE TO DETERMINE. Only the first permits judgment without a court order. If the tenant is in service, no order until the court appoints counsel; the court may require an INDEMNITY BOND as a condition of judgment. s402(c): a MANDATORY stay of at least 90 days where a defense may exist that cannot be presented without the defendant, or counsel cannot reach them. s402(e): reopening within 90 days after service ends, on showing prejudice and a meritorious defense; a bona fide purchaser's title under the judgment is protected. s402(b): a KNOWINGLY FALSE declaration is a misdemeanor (up to one year and/or $1,000) PLUS actual damages, fees and costs - so a landlord who signs a 'not in service' declaration without checking is exposed. The federal SCRA default-judgment provision (50 U.S.C. s3931) and its DoD status-verification practice were NOT read; whether CA's 120-day lookback is broader than the federal rule is not established here. Both apply. Chapter 7.5 beyond s402 remains unread, including any state lease-termination right. s403 READ 2026-09-19 (amended SB 1097, eff. 2025-01-01) - THE STAY PROVISIONS, now folded into this row so the legal tracker has a single military step. s403(a): stay of the ACTION, discretionary on the court's own motion but MANDATORY on application unless the court finds no material effect - the burden effectively runs against proceeding. s403(c)(1): stay of EXECUTION of any judgment or order - which in an unlawful detainer is the WRIT OF POSSESSION, so a landlord holding a judgment may still be unable to recover the unit. Both reach the same 120-DAY post-service window as s402(f). s403(d): up to the period of service PLUS THREE MONTHS, with installment terms possible. s403(b) BEARS ON LATE FEES: no fine or penalty accrues during a stay of an action to enforce a contract, and a court may RELIEVE a service member from a penalty incurred while in service where service materially impaired the ability to pay. A rent late fee is such a penalty. Cross-noted at late-fee-safe-harbor-ca. s403(d) last sentence: where the service member is a CODEFENDANT, the landlord may proceed against the others BY LEAVE OF COURT - relevant to multi-tenant units. s403(e): a further stay may be sought, and if refused the court must appoint counsel. s403(f): applying for a stay is not an appearance and waives no defence, including lack of personal jurisdiction. Still no state lease-TERMINATION right in ss400-403; any such right would be in s404 et seq., unread. s406 READ 2026-09-19 - THE STRONGEST LIMB, and a separate rule from the s403 stays: where premises are occupied PRIMARILY FOR DWELLING by a service member's SPOUSE, CHILDREN OR OTHER DEPENDENTS, NO EVICTION OR DISTRESS may be made during the period of service or until 120 days after release EXCEPT ON LEAVE OF COURT. So the default is BARRED, not merely stayable. On application the court shall stay, or may order partial payments, unless ability to pay is unaffected. Knowingly taking part in an eviction in breach is a MISDEMEANOR (s406(d)) plus damages and fees. s406 carries NO RENT CEILING on its face; the federal analog was not read. Where a stay is granted, the OWNER may seek reciprocal relief on its own mortgage and similar obligations (s406(b)). Also: s409.3 lets a service member petition within six months after service to defer PRE-SERVICE obligations (which can include rent under a lease signed before service), hearing within 25 days, no filing fee, no penalties or interest during deferment; s409.8 makes an officer's certificate prima facie evidence of service status - the practical evidence for the s402 declaration; s409.7 disregards transfers made to exploit the chapter; s409.14 no filing fees for service members. Chapter 7.5 now READ IN FULL.

title: Military Lease Termination
bodyText: Tenant may terminate this Lease at any time after Tenant enters military service during the Term, or, if Tenant signed this Lease while already in military service, after Tenant receives military orders for a permanent change of station or to deploy with a military unit or in support of a military operation for at least 90 days. Tenant must deliver written notice of termination and a copy of the military orders to Landlord or Landlord's agent by hand delivery, private business carrier, or mail with return receipt requested. Where rent is payable monthly, termination takes effect 30 days after the first date on which the next rent payment is due following delivery of the notice. Rent for the period before termination is prorated. Landlord will not impose any early termination charge, although Tenant remains responsible for other amounts due under this Lease at termination, including reasonable charges for excess wear. Landlord will refund any rent paid in advance for a period after termination within 30 days. Termination also ends the obligations of Tenant's dependents under this Lease. Landlord will not hold Tenant's belongings or security deposit to satisfy a claim for rent accruing after termination. If Landlord believes a request under this section is incomplete, Landlord will respond in writing within 30 days identifying what is missing.
notes: CA: Mil. & Vet. Code s409, with ss400, 401(e)(2), 409.5 and 409.15, primary text supplied by Taylor 2026-09-19 (s409 amended SB 1311, Stats. 2022 ch. 620). CALIFORNIA HAS ITS OWN MILITARY LEASE-TERMINATION RIGHT, parallel to the federal SCRA. Not required lease text, but NON-WAIVABLE (s401(e)(2) voids any waiver of a right this code gives service members), so it is shipped as a recommended clause and any base clause contradicting it fails. TRIGGERS, s409(b)(1): (A) the lessee ENTERS military service during the term; or (B) while already serving signs the lease and THEN receives PCS orders, or orders to deploy with a unit or as an individual in support of an operation, for at least 90 DAYS. Covers residential, professional, business and agricultural leases. 'Military service' is the s400 definition, which includes the STATE MILITIA on full-time active STATE service - a category the federal SCRA's scope was NOT checked against here, so whether CA is broader is flagged, not found. EFFECTIVE DATE, s409(d)(1): for monthly rent, 30 days after the first date the NEXT rent payment is due after notice is delivered; for any other lease, the last day of the month following the month of delivery. MONEY, s409(e)(1) and (f): prorated rent; NO early-termination charge; tenant still owes taxes and other lease obligations due at termination, including REASONABLE EXCESS-WEAR charges; advance rent refunded within 30 DAYS. s409(a): termination ends the obligations of the lessee's DEPENDENTS too. s409.5: dependents may themselves claim the ss405-409.4 benefits on application. CRIMINAL LIMB, s409(h): knowingly seizing or holding the tenant's belongings OR SECURITY DEPOSIT to satisfy rent accruing AFTER lawful termination is a misdemeanor (up to one year and/or $1,000). s409(g): the landlord's only route to modify the relief is a court application BEFORE the termination date. s409.15 IS THE WORKFLOW RULE: a landlord who receives a good-faith request for relief under this chapter and believes it incomplete or insufficient MUST respond in writing within 30 DAYS, identifying exactly what is missing and giving a mailing address and phone number - or it WAIVES ANY OBJECTION and the service member is entitled to the relief. A termination notice missing the orders therefore cannot simply be ignored. s409.8: a certificate from an authorized military officer is prima facie evidence of service status and dates.

title: Megan's Law website data may not be used in housing decisions
bodyText: California prohibits using information from the Megan's Law sex-offender website for purposes relating to housing or accommodations. The only authorized use of that information is to protect a person at risk of becoming a victim of a sex offense committed by the registrant. A landlord who uses it otherwise - for example, to screen out an applicant - is liable for actual damages, up to three times actual damages with a minimum of $250, attorney's fees, and exemplary damages or a civil penalty of up to $25,000, and prosecutors or an aggrieved person may sue to stop a pattern or practice of misuse. Every California lease must still tell tenants that the website exists; the landlord may point tenants to it, but may not use it to decide who to rent to.
notes: CA: Pen. Code s290.46(j), primary text read 2026-09-19 via FindLaw ('current as of January 01, 2026'; section operative 2022-01-01). ANSWERS candidate 572.6 - and runs the OPPOSITE WAY from the Ohio precedent: Ohio creates a landlord termination route for a sex offender residing near a school (s5321.051); California PROHIBITS using registry data in housing at all. s290.46(j)(1): use authorized ONLY to protect a 'person at risk'. s290.46(j)(2)(G): use 'for purposes relating to... HOUSING OR ACCOMMODATIONS' is prohibited except as (1) or another law authorizes. s290.46(j)(4)(A): actual damages; up to 3x; NOT LESS THAN $250; attorney's fees; exemplary damages OR a civil penalty up to $25,000. (j)(4)(B): pattern-or-practice injunctions by the AG, a DA, a city attorney or ANY AGGRIEVED PERSON. s290.46(h): using the information to commit a misdemeanor adds a $10,000-$50,000 fine. THE TENSION WORTH SURFACING: Civ. Code s2079.10a REQUIRES every CA lease to tell tenants about the website (sex-offender-registry-notice-ca), while s290.46(j) forbids the landlord from using it to choose tenants. Both hold. PRODUCT CONSEQUENCE: the screening workflow must NOT query the Megan's Law website or ingest its data as an eligibility input. SCOPE LIMIT: s290.46(j) restricts information 'disclosed pursuant to THIS SECTION' - i.e. the website. A sex-offense CONVICTION in a lawful consumer report is a different source, governed instead by 2 CCR ss12264-12271 (directly-related convictions only; no blanket bans). Whether a screening vendor's registry-derived field counts as 'information disclosed pursuant to this section' is NOT resolved - treat such fields as prohibited until checked. The 'person at risk' exception (defined in Pen. Code s290.45) was not read. 'PERSON AT RISK' - UNDEFINED IN THE CURRENT TEXT, read 2026-09-19: older commentary cites a definition at Pen. Code s290.45(a)(8) ('a person who is or may be exposed to a risk of becoming a victim of a sex offense committed by the offender'). The CURRENT s290.45 - repealed and re-added by SB 384, operative 2021-01-01 - contains NO such definition and no subdivision (a)(8). So the landlord's only exception in s290.46(j)(1) turns on a term whose statutory definition appears to have been dropped in the re-enactment. Another cross-reference-rot instance. Practical effect: do not build any 'person at risk' exception into the product; the prohibition is the operative rule. s290.45(e)(2) adds a $500-$1,000 fine for using s290.45 disclosures to commit a misdemeanor.

title: Unreturned deposits escheat to the state after three years
bodyText: An amount a landlord owes a former tenant - most often an unreturned security deposit refund - that the tenant has not claimed is unclaimed property under California law. If it remains unclaimed for more than three years after it became payable, it escheats to the state, and the landlord, as the holder, must report and remit it to the State Controller. Holders file an annual report before November 1 covering property escheated as of the preceding June 30.
notes: CA: CCP s1520(a) and s1530(d), read 2026-09-19 from Justia's 2025 code and FindLaw via search results. ANSWERS candidate 427.2: a CA landlord holding an unclaimed deposit refund is a HOLDER under the Unclaimed Property Law. s1520(a): intangible personal property 'held or owing in the ordinary course of the holder's business' and unclaimed for MORE THAN THREE YEARS after it became payable escheats, 'deducting any lawful charges'. s1530(d): report before NOVEMBER 1 each year as of June 30; items under $25 may be aggregated. PARTIAL, stated plainly: the holder's PRE-ESCHEAT OWNER NOTICE (which s1520's later subdivisions prescribe for deposits and accounts, with bold or larger-type content requirements), the PENALTY and INTEREST provisions, and record-retention rules were NOT read in full. Candidate 427.3 (dormancy charge as a drafting hook): s1520 permits deducting 'lawful charges', but whether a lease can create one for an unreturned deposit was NOT established - the charge provisions were not read. Note the interaction with s1950.5(h): the 21-day return duty means a refund that goes unclaimed is usually a check that was never cashed, and the three-year clock runs from when it became payable. ARTICLES 2 AND 3 READ IN FULL 2026-09-19 - the partial flags are resolved. PRE-ESCHEAT NOTICE, s1520(b): for property worth $50 OR MORE where the holder has an address, notice by mail (or electronically with consent) 6 TO 12 MONTHS before it becomes reportable, headed verbatim 'THE STATE OF CALIFORNIA REQUIRES US TO NOTIFY YOU THAT YOUR UNCLAIMED PROPERTY MAY BE TRANSFERRED TO THE STATE IF YOU DO NOT CONTACT US' (or substantially similar), with four specified statements in BOLD or at least two points larger, plus the Controller's address-confirmation form; owner contact restarts the escheat period; a notice charge of no more than $2. DORMANCY CHARGES - candidate 427.3 RESOLVED, and it is the OPPOSITE of North Dakota: s1520(d) defines 'lawful charges' as those authorized by statute or a valid contract, BUT s1522 bars deducting ANY charge 'imposed because of the inactive or unclaimed status' unless THIS CHAPTER specifically permits it - and even then not if the holder would not have deducted it had the owner claimed in time. The only chapter-permitted charge is the $2 notice fee. So a lease clause creating a dormancy charge on an unclaimed deposit is ineffective in California. REPORT AND REMIT: s1530(d) report before NOVEMBER 1 as of June 30, verified by the holder (s1530(e)); names and addresses for items of $25 or more, smaller items aggregated. s1532(a): remit no sooner than SEVEN MONTHS and no later than seven months and 15 days after the report deadline; cash of $2,000 or more by EFT, with a 2% civil penalty for paying otherwise (s1532(h)). s1532(b): if the owner claims before remittance, pay the owner and file a report instead. STILL UNREAD: the s1577 interest provision that s1532(c) references, and the late-reporting penalty sections. GROUP NORMALISED 2026-09-19: 'Security Deposits' -> 'Security Deposit' (session drift; 12 canonical groups are used by all nine states).

title: After judgment: the writ of possession and occupant claims
bodyText: In California a judgment for possession is enforced by a writ of possession executed by the sheriff or marshal. The officer serves the writ on an occupant, or posts it and serves the tenant, and the occupants then have five days to leave; that period cannot be extended. If the officer does not execute the writ within three court days, a registered process server may. An occupant not named in the judgment who was living there when the case was filed may file a claim of right to possession, which stops the eviction pending a hearing, unless a prejudgment claim form was served on all occupants with the summons. Personal property left behind after the landlord takes possession must be stored and may be reclaimed within 15 days on payment of reasonable storage costs, after which it is sold or disposed of under the abandoned-property procedure. A tenant's bankruptcy filing does not delay execution of the possession writ, and a forfeiture judgment does not end the tenant's liability for damages.
notes: CA: CCP ss715.010-715.050 and 1174(d)-(m), 1174.3, 1174.25, 1174.5, primary text supplied by Taylor 2026-09-19. ANSWERS candidates 367.3 and 367.5. A LEGAL-TRACKER row. TIMING: s715.020(c) - FIVE DAYS from service on an occupant (or on the judgment debtor where posted), and CCP s684.120 time extensions expressly DO NOT apply. s715.040: if the sheriff or marshal does not execute within THREE court days, a registered process server may. No daylight-only or SSI/SSDI extension of the Colorado kind was found. s715.050: execution proceeds WITHOUT DELAY notwithstanding notice of the tenant's BANKRUPTCY filing, except as to money judgments and mobilehome writs. OCCUPANT CLAIMS: s715.020(d) bars removing an unnamed person who claims possession predating the action, UNLESS a PREJUDGMENT claim of right to possession was served on all occupants under CCP s415.46 (NOT READ) - so serving the prejudgment form with the summons is what closes this gap, and the tracker should prompt for it. s1174.3: a claim at the writ stage stops the eviction on the spot; the claimant deposits 15 days' rent (or proceeds without it on a fee waiver) and a hearing follows in 5-15 days. s1174.25: a prejudgment claimant has 10 days to file and is added as a defendant. PROPERTY: s715.010(b)(3) and s715.030 route post-writ property through s1174(e)-(m) - 15 DAYS to reclaim on payment of storage costs, lost property to police under s2080 et seq., non-tenant owners noticed under Civ. Code s1983, disposal under s1988, with liability shields paralleling s1989. s1174(h) also references Civ. Code s1965 (NOT READ). SERVICE-MEMBER tenants: storage liens need a court order first (Mil. & Vet. Code s409.1(b)). s1174.5: a forfeiture judgment does NOT relieve s1951.2 damages liability.

title: Subletting and Assignment (Landlord's Sole Discretion)
bodyText: Tenant will not sublease or assign all or any portion of the property or this Lease without Landlord's prior written consent, which Landlord may grant or withhold in Landlord's sole discretion. Tenant will not rent the property, or any portion of it, on any short-term rental or home-sharing platform.
notes: CA: ALTERNATIVE to no-sublet-assign-ca, CHOICE GROUP 'ca-sublet-consent' - a CA lease must contain EXACTLY ONE. Lawful in CA: nothing read prohibits a sole-discretion consent standard in a residential lease. THE TRADE-OFF, Civ. Code s1951.4: the continue-the-lease remedy (keep the lease alive after the tenant breaches and abandons, and recover rent as it falls due) is available ONLY if the lease permits subletting or assignment, or conditions it on reasonable standards, or on consent 'not unreasonably withheld' (s1951.4(b)(1)-(3)). Sole discretion satisfies none of the three, so choosing this option FORFEITS s1951.4 and leaves the landlord with s1951.2 termination damages after abandonment - the landlord must terminate, and the tenant may reduce recovery by proving rental loss that could reasonably have been avoided. Both options remain subject to s1947.12(c) (a sublease may not exceed the lawful rent) and s1946.2(b)(1)(G) (an unauthorized sublet or assignment is at-fault just cause). Local ordinances limiting refusal of replacement roommates are municipal and out of scope. SHIPPED INACTIVE: the builder cannot yet express 'choose one of these two'. If both rows were active, a CA lease would contain both, contradicting itself. Activate this row once the builder supports choice groups; the default stays active. ACTIVATED 2026-09-19 now that choice_group/is_default exist: the row was held inactive only because the schema could not say 'exactly one of these'. It is an alternative within choice_group 'ca-sublet-consent', is_default=FALSE. GROUP NORMALISED 2026-09-19: 'Property Use' -> 'Tenant Responsibilities'.

title: Choosing a subletting consent standard
bodyText: A California landlord can require its consent to any sublease or assignment, and must choose how that consent works. Under the reasonable-consent standard, the landlord may refuse only for a reasonable reason - a prospective subtenant's poor credit or rental history, for example - and must be prepared to justify a refusal. In exchange, if the tenant later breaks the lease and moves out, the landlord may keep the lease in force and collect rent as it comes due for the rest of the term. Under the sole-discretion standard, the landlord may refuse for any lawful reason and keeps full control over who lives in the property, but gives up that remedy: if the tenant breaks the lease and moves out, the landlord must end the lease and sue for its losses, and the tenant can reduce what they owe by showing the landlord could have re-rented the unit. Either way, a sublease cannot charge more than the lawful rent, a refusal can never be based on a protected characteristic, and an unauthorized sublease is grounds for eviction.
notes: CA: the landlord-facing explanation for CHOICE GROUP 'ca-sublet-consent' - show at the point of selection. Sources: Civ. Code ss1951.4(b), 1951.2(a)(2)-(3) and (c), 1947.12(c), 1946.2(b)(1)(G); fair-housing limits under Gov. Code s12955. Written plainly for a landlord choosing between no-sublet-assign-ca (default) and no-sublet-assign-discretion-ca. GROUP NORMALISED 2026-09-19: 'Property Use' -> 'Tenant Responsibilities' (session drift; 12 canonical groups are used by all nine states).

title: Possession Delay
bodyText: If Landlord is unable to deliver possession of the property to Tenant on the Start Date, Tenant will not owe Monthly Rent for any period before possession is delivered. If Tenant terminates this Lease because Landlord did not deliver possession, as permitted by the Damage, Destruction and Failure to Deliver section of this Lease, Landlord will return all amounts Tenant paid to Landlord.
notes: CA: override of possession-delay, built 2026-09-19 after the overlap check found the base row's 30-DAY termination window in conflict with casualty-termination-ca, which states Civ. Code s1932(1): the tenant may terminate if the landlord does not, WITHIN A REASONABLE TIME AFTER REQUEST, place and secure the tenant in quiet possession. Two rules for one event in the same lease invites exactly the dispute a lease should prevent, and the 30-day narrowing was lawful only if the lease was presented before possession (s1953(b)) - a dependency the builder cannot track. This override keeps the base row's tenant-favorable terms (no rent before possession; full refund on termination) and DEFERS the termination right to casualty-termination-ca, cross-referenced by that row's title. The refund is contractual: Civ. Code s1941.9(a)'s 21-day return of advance rent is keyed to s1932(2) and s1933(4), not s1932(1).

title: Maintenance & Repairs
bodyText: Subject to Tenant's own maintenance obligations under this Lease, Landlord will maintain the property, including its structural elements, roof, and systems, in good order and repair, and will be responsible for repairing the appliances, fixtures, and equipment located at the property, except where repair is necessary due to improper use by Tenant or a guest of Tenant. Tenant will notify Landlord promptly of any condition requiring repair or maintenance; notice may be given orally or in writing, though written notice is encouraged. Landlord will undertake required repairs within a reasonable time, consistent with applicable law.
notes: CA: override of landlord-maintenance (a generic row currently tagged CO only), built 2026-09-19. Needed for two reasons found in the whole-library re-audit. (1) CROSS-REFERENCE: appliances-included, tagged CA, commits the landlord to maintain appliances 'as described in this Lease's Maintenance & Repairs Section' - without this row a CA lease had no such section. (2) ONE CA CONFLICT in the base text: it requires the tenant to give repair notice 'in writing'. Civ. Code s1942(a) triggers the landlord's repair duty and the tenant's repair-and-deduct remedy on 'written or oral notice', and s1942.1 voids any agreement modifying s1942 rights. The override permits either and encourages writing. Otherwise the text tracks s1941 (landlord duty) and the s1929/s1941.2 tenant-misuse exception. Note s1941.7: the mold repair duty arises only on notice. The base row sits in the open CO/WY maintenance-clause backlog; if that work changes it, re-check this override.

title: Storage Space
bodyText: Tenant is assigned the following storage space for Tenant's exclusive use during the Term: [identify storage space/location here]. Tenant will not store any hazardous, flammable, or perishable materials in the storage space.
notes: MERGED 2026-09-19 from storage-space-ks, storage-space-oh, storage-space-ca — bodies BYTE-IDENTICAL, same rule_type. Each state reached this clause by deleting the same liability-limiting sentence under its own exculpation ban (K.S.A. 58-2547(a)(4); ORC 5321.13(D); Civ. Code 1953(a)(5) with Henrioulle and Whitehead), so three ids held one clause. NE and MN keep separate rows - their texts differ. METADATA RECONCILED: group and title taken from the parent row 'storage-space' (Parking & Storage / Storage Space); the merged sources disagreed - groups ['Parking & Storage', 'Storage'], titles ['Storage Space', 'Storage Space (Ohio)'] - including an Ohio title carrying '(Ohio)', a convention no other state uses. Per-state reasoning preserved below. || [KS] K.S.A. 58-2547(a)(4). Conservative fix (Taylor's decision, session 5): drops the liability-limiting language entirely rather than rely on K.S.A. 58-2547(a)(4)'s narrow exception (tenant agreeing to limit landlord's liability for fire, theft, or breakage in common areas). That exception might arguably cover some of this clause's content, but whether an assigned/exclusive-use space counts as a 'common area' is an untested interpretive question — not worth guessing on for a live product. Documented here as an alternative worth a real attorney's review if Taylor wants to revisit a narrower fix later. Storage space assigned for Tenant's exclusive use is a weaker fit for the 'common area' exception than parking would be, if that argument is ever revisited. | REVIEWED 2026-09-07 (cross-state follow-up), NO CHANGE. Not changed; flagged. || [OH] OH: §5321.13(D) bars any tenant agreement to the exculpation or limitation of any liability of the landlord arising under law. Unlike K.S.A. 58-2547(a)(4), Ohio's ban carries NO common-areas exception, so the conservative fix (drop the liability-limiting sentence entirely) is required here rather than merely prudent. FOUND ON RE-SCREEN 2026-09-18 - missed in the first Ohio liability pass. | NV: Read in full 2026-09-24 against NRS 118A (revisor text Rev. 4/15/2026, 2025 session incorporated). Applies as written. The property will be left in the same condition as at the start of the Term, except for ordinary wear and tear, and free of all personal property of Tenant and any occupants. Personal property left at the property after Tenant vacates will be handled as described in this Lease's provision governing property abandoned after termination.

title: No state duty to pay interest on deposits
bodyText: California imposes no statewide requirement to pay interest on a security deposit or to hold it in a separate interest-bearing account. Some California cities do require deposit interest by ordinance, so a landlord should check local rules for the city where the property is located.
notes: CA: CONFIRMED ABSENT. Civ. Code s1950.5 was read section-open IN FULL and contains no interest requirement anywhere - not in (b) permitted purposes, (c) the cap, (e) deductions, or (h) return mechanics. Proof-of-absence from the governing statute read end to end, not an inference from silence. Municipal layer flagged and NOT resolved - several CA cities impose deposit interest by ordinance; see edu-municipal-layer-ca. Row added 2026-09-19 for consistency with the confirmed-absence rows other states ship (edu-no-deposit-installments-ks etc.); the finding itself dates from the s1950.5 read earlier in the pass. GROUP NORMALISED 2026-09-19: 'Security Deposits' -> 'Security Deposit' (session drift; 12 canonical groups are used by all nine states).

title: No joint move-in inventory requirement
bodyText: California does not require a joint, signed move-in condition inventory. It substitutes two different mechanisms: the tenant may request an initial inspection during the final two weeks of the tenancy, and for tenancies beginning on or after July 1, 2025 the landlord must photograph the unit at the start of the tenancy.
notes: CA: CONFIRMED ABSENT as a joint signed instrument, from Civ. Code s1950.5 read in full. What CA has instead is s1950.5(f) (tenant-requested INITIAL INSPECTION in the final two weeks - a move-OUT device) and s1950.5(g)(1) (landlord PHOTOGRAPHS at the start of tenancies beginning on or after 2025-07-01). A canvass looking for the usual joint-inventory shape would record 'absent' and miss that CA covers the same ground unilaterally. See security-deposit-return-ca. GROUP NORMALISED 2026-09-19: 'Property Condition' -> 'Landlord Responsibilities' (session drift; 12 canonical groups are used by all nine states).

title: No right to pay the deposit in installments
bodyText: California gives tenants no statutory right to pay a security deposit in installments. The statutory cap reduces the need for one: since July 1, 2024 security may not exceed one month's rent for most landlords.
notes: CA: CONFIRMED ABSENT from Civ. Code s1950.5 read in full - no installment or payment-plan right appears anywhere. Note s1950.5(c)(1) caps security at ONE MONTH'S RENT from 2024-07-01 (two months for the small-owner exception at (c)(5), disapplied for service members). Municipal ordinances not screened. See security-deposit-cap-ca. GROUP NORMALISED 2026-09-19: 'Security Deposits' -> 'Security Deposit' (session drift; 12 canonical groups are used by all nine states).

title: No radon disclosure requirement
bodyText: California has no statute requiring a residential landlord to test for radon or to disclose radon to tenants. The state's radon provision addresses construction standards for new buildings rather than landlord duties, and California's Proposition 65 warning requirement does not reach radon, because radon is not on the state's list of chemicals known to cause cancer or reproductive toxicity. A known radon problem can still matter: conditions severe enough to affect habitability run through the ordinary habitability rules, and a landlord who conceals a known hazard can face liability on other grounds.
notes: CA: CONFIRMED ABSENT FROM THE GOVERNING TITLE, with the scope stated. Civ. Code Title 5 Chapters 1-2 (ss1925-1954.071) were swept end to end 2026-09-19 and contain no radon provision. This is NOT a whole-code proof: a radon duty outside Title 5 - in the Health and Safety Code, say - was not searched for. Recorded at that strength deliberately, since CA's disclosure duties are scattered across at least four codes. | CA 2026-09-24 follow-up: NOT CLOSED - set to NEEDS_REVIEW. Searched: CDPH Radon Program 'Radon and Real Estate' page (points to natural-hazard disclosure sections and the Residential Environmental Hazards booklet; no rental disclosure duty), targeted searches for a CA radon landlord disclosure/testing statute (secondary sources only, all saying none), practitioner lists of CA required disclosures (radon absent from all). Consistent but not primary. NEW LEAD: Proposition 65 (H&S s25249.6) requires a business to warn before knowingly exposing anyone to a listed chemical, and OEHHA has residential-rental safe-harbor warnings (27 CCR ss25607.34-25607.35). Whether radon is on the Prop 65 list is UNVERIFIED; if it is, a landlord above the employee threshold who knows of a radon exposure may owe a warning. bodyText narrowed to the interim text pending that check. To close, needed (ranges): the H&S chapter TOC for CDPH's indoor-radon provisions (Div. 103/104); the current OEHHA Prop 65 list entry for radon (list dated 2023-12-29 or later); 27 CCR Art. 6, ss25600-25607.35; H&S ss25249.6 and 25249.11. | CA 2026-09-24 second follow-up: CLOSED, back to VERIFIED. Three independent routes, all negative: (1) Civ. Code Title 5 Chs. 1-2 read end to end - no radon provision; (2) H&S s105430 (Div. 103, Pt. 5, Ch. 7, Indoor Environmental Quality) is the radon provision and governs construction standards for NEW BUILDINGS and a radon assessment/mitigation plan conditioning building permits - no landlord, tenancy, disclosure or testing duty; s105430(e) makes (a)-(d) operative only if federal funds are available (same contingent-commencement shape as H&S s26147 for mold); (3) Prop 65 closed at the list - s25249.6 reaches only chemicals on the s25249.8 list, and the OEHHA list (dated 2023-12-29) has no radon entry; s25249.11(b) would exclude landlords under 10 employees regardless. SCOPE: confirmed absent from those three routes; Div. 103 and 104 were selected by part/article title, not read in full - not a whole-code proof.

title: Proposition 65 Rental Property Warnings
bodyText: A California landlord with ten or more employees must give tenants a Proposition 65 warning before knowingly exposing them to a chemical the state lists as causing cancer or reproductive harm. In rental housing these are typically tobacco smoke, engine exhaust, carbon monoxide, lead or asbestos. The warning goes to each known adult occupant when the property is rented and again every year after that. It may be delivered by letter addressed to each known adult occupant, by email to the addresses the landlord otherwise uses to reach them, or in the lease itself - but a warning given in the lease covers only the adults who sign it or are named in it, so other occupants still need a letter or email. If the lease or any other required notice is given in another language, the warning must be given in that language too. The regulation prescribes the wording, which names the exposure source and the chemical, tells the tenant to talk to the landlord about how and when exposure could occur, and directs them to www.P65Warnings.ca.gov/apartments. Properties with an enclosed parking facility or a designated smoking area need separate warnings for those areas. Violations carry civil penalties of up to $2,500 per day, and private parties may sue after giving 60 days' notice.
notes: CA: H&S ss25249.6, 25249.11(b) and 27 CCR ss25607.34-25607.35, read 2026-09-24 (Claude Desktop follow-up, primary text supplied by Taylor). Surfaced while closing the radon row - radon is not on the Prop 65 list, but the residential-rental warning regime it sits in IS a real CA landlord duty the library had no row for in any state. Trigger is a knowing exposure to a LISTED chemical (s25249.8 list), by a landlord employing 10 OR MORE (s25249.11(b)); s25249.10(c) exempts exposures posing no significant risk, WITH THE BURDEN ON THE LANDLORD, and s25249.10(b) gives a 12-month grace after a chemical is listed. THE ANNUAL REPETITION IN s25607.34(b) IS THE REQUIREMENT LANDLORDS MISS - the duty is not discharged at move-in. Lease delivery under (b)(3) is the weakest method: it binds only signers and named adults, and in a renewal year covers only that year. s25607.34(c) language duty attaches to any language used for the lease or other required notices - cross-refer Civ. Code s1632. s25607.34(d) requires separate enclosed-parking (ss25607.20-.21) and designated-smoking-area (ss25607.28-.29) warnings. Content per s25607.35 includes the s25603(a)(1) symbol - s25603 NOT READ, so the symbol specification is unverified. Article 6 is SAFE HARBOUR ONLY: s25600(a) says nothing in it determines whether a warning is required, and s25600(f) permits other compliant wording. Enforcement: s25249.7(b)(1) up to $2,500 per day per violation; (c) AG, DA or city attorney; (d) private enforcement 60 days after notice with a certificate of merit. s25249.7(k)(1)(C)-(D): for environmental tobacco smoke on premises where smoking is permitted, and engine exhaust inside a parking facility, a landlord can cut off a private action once by correcting within 14 days and paying a $500 penalty (CPI-adjusted every five years) - a genuine safe harbour worth surfacing in the tracker. Regulations filed 2019-03-12, operative 2019-07-01.

title: Proposition 65 Warning
bodyText: WARNING: [Name of one or more exposure sources] on this property can expose you to chemicals including [name of one or more chemicals] which are known to the State of California to cause cancer. Talk to your landlord or the building owner about how and when you could be exposed to these chemicals in your building. For additional information go to www.P65Warnings.ca.gov/apartments.
notes: CA: 27 CCR s25607.35 safe-harbor content (single-carcinogen variant), usable as lease delivery under s25607.34(b)(3). SHIPPED INACTIVE 2026-09-24, pending Taylor's decision and three builder gaps: (1) the regulation supplies four other variants (single carcinogen, reproductive toxicants, both, and a chemical listed as both) - the builder must pick by chemical category rather than hardcode this one; (2) the warning must carry the s25603(a)(1) symbol, and s25603 has NOT been read; (3) a lease warning covers only signers and named adults and only that year - the letter-or-email path for other occupants and the annual repeat still need a workflow. See edu-prop65-rental-warning-ca.

title: No special rule for postdated checks
bodyText: California's bad-check statute contains no exception or special rule for postdated checks. What it does contain is a certified-mail demand procedure that raises a landlord's recovery from a service charge to treble the amount of the check, subject to a good-faith-dispute defence where the tenant stopped payment.
notes: CA: CONFIRMED ABSENT from Civ. Code s1719 read IN FULL 2026-09-19 - no postdated-check exclusion in any subdivision. The trap other states carry (a postdated check forfeiting bad-check remedies) does not exist here. The real mechanics are in nsf-fee-limit-ca: s1719(a)(2) treble damages ($100-$1,500) after a certified-mail demand and 30 days; s1719(a)(3) good-faith-dispute defence on a stop payment, which the payee must rebut by clear and convincing evidence; (a)(4) bank error and (a)(5) delayed benefit-deposit exceptions. Scope caveat stands: s1719 reaches a 'check, draft, or order', not ACH or card.

title: Total Monthly Rent Disclosure
bodyText: The Monthly Rent of {{monthly_rent}} stated in this Lease is the maximum total amount of periodic rent due under this Lease and includes every mandatory fee Tenant must pay in addition to base rent. Landlord will not charge Tenant periodic rent greater than this amount. [Include only if a utility exception applies, as a statement on the same page as the Monthly Rent figure, keyed to it by an asterisk or other reference symbol at least half the font size of that figure: "*The [electric / natural gas / water] service in your unit is not included in the Monthly Rent. {{utility_provider_name}} ({{utility_provider_phone}}) is unable to contract with you directly for that service, so the monthly bill for the service provided in your unit will be charged to you as a separate monthly fee equal to the cost of that bill." For a master-metered water system instead: "*This unit is served by a master-metered water system. A fee for water service will be charged to you as a separate monthly fee equal to the cost of the water service provided in your unit."]
notes: NV: Section-open read of revisor text (leg.state.nv.us, Rev. 4/15/2026). NRS 118A.200(6)-(8), added 2025 (Stats. 2025 pp. 1413, 1990 per the section history - enactment evidenced by codification). (6) wherever rent is listed or referenced it must be a SINGLE figure = maximum total periodic rent INCLUDING mandatory fees; (7) may not charge more; (8) the only carve-outs: a utility the public utility cannot contract for directly, or master-metered water, each requiring an asterisk/reference symbol not less than half the font size of the single figure, tied to a statement ON THE SAME PAGE. 118A.405 (2025): tenant action for damages, equitable relief, costs and fees, plus $250 statutory damages per violation involving deception. 118A.200(9): a nonconforming agreement is unlawful to use and a contravening provision is void. SCHEMA GAP: font-size and same-page placement - same class as CA's type-size floors. BUILDER: every mandatory monthly fee (pet fee, portal fee if mandatory, amenity fee) must roll into {{monthly_rent}}. effective_from left blank: the session-law effective-date sections were not read.  | NV (text batch 2, 2026-09-24): effective_from 2025-10-01: AB 121 (2025) enrolled text read on the Legislature archive - it contains NO effective-date section, so the Oct. 1 default applies (NRS 218D.330, not itself read; corroborated by the NELIS chapter note "Chapter 227, effective October 1, 2025" as reported by BillTrack50).

title: Late Fee
bodyText: If Tenant fails to pay Monthly Rent in full within {{late_fee_grace_days}} days after it is due, a late fee of {{late_fee_amount}} will be assessed. No late fee will be charged until at least 3 calendar days after the date rent is due. The late fee for any late payment will not exceed 5 percent of the Monthly Rent, and the maximum late fee will not be increased based on any late fee previously imposed. Acceptance of a late payment does not waive Landlord's right to require full payment of Rent on the date it is due or to pursue any other remedy available under this Lease.
notes: NV: Section-open read of revisor text (leg.state.nv.us, Rev. 4/15/2026). NRS 118A.210(4) (A. 2019, 2021): reasonable late fee as set forth in the rental agreement; in a tenancy longer than week to week no late fee until at least 3 calendar days after due; must not exceed 5% of periodic rent; maximum must not be increased based on a previously imposed late fee. Builder constraints: {{late_fee_grace_days}} >= 3; {{late_fee_amount}} <= 5% of {{monthly_rent}} (the all-in figure, 118A.125/.200(6)). 118A.150: rent includes reasonable and actual late fees in the agreement. 118A.355(1)(d)/.380(1)(c): withholding tenants incur no late fee. Waiver-by-acceptance sentence kept from base; no NV waiver statute located in 118A (Ch. 40 not read). Supersedes late-fee for NV rather than tagging it: base states no cap and NV's three limits are hard statutory numbers.

title: Limit on Total Security
bodyText: The total amount or value of all security deposits and any surety bond under this Lease, including any Monthly Rent paid in advance for the last month of the Term and any pet or cleaning deposit, will not exceed three months' Monthly Rent. Tenant may, if Landlord consents, purchase a surety bond in place of all or part of the Security Deposit; Landlord is not required to accept one and will not require Tenant to purchase one.
notes: NV: Section-open read of revisor text (leg.state.nv.us, Rev. 4/15/2026). NRS 118A.242(1)-(3); 118A.240(1)-(2) (A. 2021). "Security deposit" = any payment, deposit, fee or charge used to remedy rent default, repair non-normal-wear damage, or clean - so pet and cleaning deposits count toward the cap; excludes an option-to-purchase payment and a surety-bond premium. 118A.242(5): tenant may dispute an itemized accounting to the surety within 30 days; surety may not credit-report absent judgment. Does NOT supersede security-deposit-use (CA's cap row did; that would strip NV of the use clause). Builder constraint: sum of deposit fields <= 3 x {{monthly_rent}}.

title: Security Deposit Return
bodyText: Upon termination of the tenancy by either party for any reason, Landlord may claim from the Security Deposit, or any surety bond, only amounts reasonably necessary to remedy Tenant's default in paying Rent, to repair damage to the property caused by Tenant other than normal wear, and to pay the reasonable costs of cleaning. No later than 30 days after the termination of the tenancy, Landlord will provide Tenant an itemized, written accounting of the disposition of the Security Deposit and any surety bond, and will return any remaining portion of the Security Deposit by handing it to Tenant personally at the place where Rent is paid or by mailing it to Tenant's present address or, if that address is unknown, Tenant's last known address. Except for any nonrefundable cleaning charge in a reasonable amount stated in this Lease, no part of the Security Deposit is nonrefundable. Tenant is asked to give Landlord a forwarding address in writing.
notes: NV: Section-open read of revisor text (leg.state.nv.us, Rev. 4/15/2026). NRS 118A.242(4), (6)-(9) (A. 2021). Deadline: 30 days after termination of tenancy (no forwarding-address trigger; clause only ASKS for one). Delivery: personally at place rent is paid, or mail to present/last known address. Penalty 118A.242(6)-(7): liable for the entire deposit plus up to the amount of the entire deposit, court weighing good faith, course of conduct and harm. (8): only a reasonable nonrefundable CLEANING charge may be carved out; any waiver/modification of s242 rights void. (9): tenant's claim has priority over landlord's creditors. 118A.350(3)/.355(3)/.370(1)/.390(3)/.400(2): deposit returnable on those terminations; 118A.345(5): no withholding for DV early termination. INSTRUCTION 24 FAMILY: closes NV's gap in the security-deposit-return REQUIRED family.

title: Move-In Inventory and Condition Record
bodyText: Landlord and Tenant have completed and signed a written record of the inventory and condition of the premises under Tenant's exclusive custody and control. That signed record is attached to and forms part of this Lease.
notes: NV: Section-open read of revisor text (leg.state.nv.us, Rev. 4/15/2026). NRS 118A.200(3)(k): any written rental agreement MUST contain "a signed record of the inventory and condition of the premises under the exclusive custody and control of the tenant." Unlike K.S.A. 58-2548 (joint, within 5 days after start) NV sets no window - the record is lease content, so it must exist at execution. Why not massage move-in-inventory-ks: its 5-day post-start window is Kansas statute and would put the NV record outside the executed agreement. BUILDER: signed attachment needed before the lease is final.

title: Manager, Agent and Owner Disclosure
bodyText: Persons authorized to manage the premises: {{manager_name}}, {{manager_address}}. Person within the state authorized to act for Landlord for service of process and for receiving notices and demands: {{owner_agent_name}}, {{owner_agent_address}}. Principal or corporate owner: {{owner_name}}, {{owner_address}}. Emergency telephone number of a responsible person who resides in the county, or within 60 miles, where the premises are located: {{emergency_phone}}. Landlord will keep this information current.
notes: NV: Section-open read of revisor text (leg.state.nv.us, Rev. 4/15/2026). NRS 118A.260(1)-(2) (A. 2007): in writing at or before commencement; agent for process must be WITHIN THE STATE; emergency contact must reside in the county or within 60 miles. 118A.260(3)-(5): a party who signs for the landlord without complying becomes the landlord's agent for process and obligations; undisclosed landlord remains liable. 118A.270: alternative - posted notices (every elevator plus one conspicuous place, or two conspicuous places). 118A.410: after tenant demand, actual damages or $25, whichever greater. Separate from landlord-identity-oh / -ks / -ne / -mn because none carries the in-state agent or 60-mile emergency contact.

title: Delay in Delivering Possession
bodyText: If Landlord fails to deliver possession of the property to Tenant as required by this Lease, Rent abates until possession is delivered, and Tenant may: (a) terminate this Lease on at least 5 days' written notice to Landlord, in which case Landlord will return all prepaid Rent, the Security Deposit to the extent recoverable by Tenant, and any payment, deposit, fee or charge made to secure the execution of this Lease; (b) demand performance of this Lease and, if Tenant elects, bring an action for possession against Landlord or any person wrongfully in possession and recover actual damages, except that Landlord is not liable for damages if Landlord exercised due diligence to evict a holdover tenant or remedy the condition keeping Tenant from taking possession; or (c) pursue any other remedy available to Tenant, including recovery of actual damages.
notes: NV: Section-open read of revisor text (leg.state.nv.us, Rev. 4/15/2026). NRS 118A.370 (A. 2021). Base possession-delay conflicts: it keeps the lease "in full force" and allows termination only after 30 days, while 118A.370(1) lets the tenant terminate on 5 days' notice at any time possession is not delivered - and 118A.220(1)(a) voids a waiver of chapter rights. possession-delay-ks/-ne are close but carry KS 1.5x / NE 3x willful-failure penalties NV lacks, so they cannot be shared. 118A.280: duty to deliver at commencement in habitable condition.

title: Tenant Maintenance Obligations
bodyText: Tenant will: keep the part of the premises Tenant occupies and uses as clean and safe as the condition of the premises permits; dispose of all ashes, garbage, rubbish and other waste from the dwelling unit in a clean and safe manner; keep all plumbing fixtures in the dwelling unit as clean as their condition permits; use all electrical, plumbing, sanitary, heating, ventilating, air-conditioning and other facilities and appliances, including elevators, in a reasonable manner; not deliberately or negligently render the premises uninhabitable or destroy, deface, damage, impair or remove any part of the premises, or knowingly permit any person to do so; and conduct himself or herself, and require other persons on the premises with Tenant's consent to conduct themselves, in a manner that will not disturb a neighbor's peaceful enjoyment of the premises. Tenant will pay for repairs, maintenance or other work needed because of a condition caused by the deliberate or negligent act or omission of Tenant, a member of Tenant's household, or another person on the premises with Tenant's consent.
notes: NV: Section-open read of revisor text (leg.state.nv.us, Rev. 4/15/2026). NRS 118A.310(1)(b)-(g) near-verbatim; last sentence from 118A.290(5) (A. 2023). Supersedes base tenant-maintenance for NV: the base's "maintain the property in the same condition as it was delivered" imposes a repair duty regardless of fault, which collides with 118A.290(4) (no fee or charge for repairs that are the landlord's duty, including home-warranty deductibles/copays, 2023) and 118A.220(1)(a). Same structure as CA's override (tenant-maintenance-obligations-ca, s1941.2); KS/NE/ND tenant-duties rows carry their own statutes' code-compliance limb that 118A.310 lacks.

title: Pet Policy
bodyText: Tenant may keep only pets identified in writing to and approved by Landlord: [list approved pets, or state that no pets are permitted]. Any pet deposit is part of the Security Deposit, is refundable as provided in this Lease, and counts toward the limit on total security. Any monthly pet fee is a mandatory fee included in the Monthly Rent stated in this Lease and is not charged in addition to it. Tenant is responsible for all damage, waste removal, odor, and disturbance caused by a pet. Landlord may revoke approval of a pet that becomes a nuisance or safety concern. Landlord may enter the property in connection with a pet only as permitted by this Lease's Access & Entry terms and applicable law, including without notice in an emergency. This Section does not apply to an assistance animal.
notes: NV: Section-open read of revisor text (leg.state.nv.us, Rev. 4/15/2026). Every existing pet-policy row fails NV somewhere: base/-sd indemnity reaches the landlord's own negligence (118A.220(1)(d)); base/-ne "without liability" exculpation; base/-ks/-ne non-emergency entry to remove a pet is not an access purpose 118A.330 allows ((4): no other right of access); and every row prices pet rent OUTSIDE the rent figure, which 118A.200(6) (2025) forbids for a mandatory fee. 118A.200(3)(c): lease must address occupancy by pets. 118A.240: pet deposit = security deposit (cap 118A.242(1)). 118A.320(1)(g): a later rule may not take away a pet right before the agreement ends. Assistance-animal carve-out deliberately generic - NRS 118.105 not yet read (see log). | NV (text batch 2, 2026-09-24): NRS 118.105 now read (host): the assistance-animal carve-out stands; state law covers animals that "assist, support or provide service".

title: Payment Methods
bodyText: Rent and other amounts due under this Lease may be paid by the following methods: [list accepted payment methods]. At least one listed method does not require Tenant to pay any fee or charge for using it or to provide information about a bank account of Tenant (payment by a check that contains such information is permitted). If Tenant may pay through an Internet website or online portal, the fee Landlord charges Tenant for using it is [state amount, or "none"], which does not exceed the fee charged by the operator of the website or portal. Landlord may change the accepted methods on reasonable written notice, but will always keep at least one method that meets the requirements of this Section.
notes: NV: Section-open read of revisor text (leg.state.nv.us, Rev. 4/15/2026). NRS 118A.303 (2025, Stats. p. 1412). (1): at least one method with no fee AND no bank-account information (check exception). (2): portal fee capped at operator's fee AND must be separately identified in any written rental agreement. Supersedes acceptable-payment-methods for NV (as payment-methods-ca does for CA). CONSOLIDATION CONSIDERED AND REJECTED: writing the fee-free-method promise into the base would impose a new obligation on landlords in eight states that do not require it (a product change, not a uniform clarification); a vague "if law requires" hedge would leave the NV portal-fee disclosure unmet. effective_from left blank: the session-law effective-date sections were not read.  | NV (text batch 2, 2026-09-24): effective_from 2025-10-01: AB 121 (2025) enrolled text read on the Legislature archive - it contains NO effective-date section, so the Oct. 1 default applies (NRS 218D.330, not itself read; corroborated by the NELIS chapter note "Chapter 227, effective October 1, 2025" as reported by BillTrack50).  | NV (research pass, 2026-09-24): Research pass on 118A.303(1)(a): unresolved (see returned-payments-nv). Safe product default: a fee-free way to pay by personal check (in person or by mail) should always be among the listed methods; do not rely on money orders or cashier's checks as the only compliant method.

title: Returned Payments
bodyText: If any payment of Rent is returned for insufficient funds or otherwise fails, Tenant will pay a returned-payment charge of [state amount; $25 or less], not to exceed the maximum amount permitted by applicable law. Landlord may then require that the payment be replaced by a cashier's check, certified check, money order, or another payment method that does not require Tenant to pay a fee or provide bank account information. If more than two of Tenant's payments during the Term are returned for insufficient funds, Landlord may require all future payments to be made by those methods. Landlord will continue to accept at least one method of payment that does not require Tenant to pay a fee or provide bank account information.
notes: NV: Section-open read of revisor text (leg.state.nv.us, Rev. 4/15/2026). Supersedes returned-payments for NV. Two NV conflicts in the base: (1) 118A.200(3)(g) requires the lease to state charges for return of a dishonored check - base leaves the amount unstated; (2) restricting a tenant to cashier's/certified check/money order - each normally carrying an issuer fee, and certified checks a bank account - risks removing the fee-free, no-bank-information method 118A.303(1) requires. AMBIGUITY FLAGGED (research-mode trigger: ambiguous statute language): whether an issuer's fee is a "fee or charge for using the method" under 118A.303(1)(a); the clause is drafted to be lawful on either reading. OPEN: NV dishonored-check charge cap is outside 118A and not yet located; clause defers to it. | NV (research pass, 2026-09-24): Research pass: NRS 597.960 caps a seller's dishonored-check fee at $25 for goods or services (reach to rent unsettled) - the bracket now steers to $25 or less as the safe figure. NRS 41.620 civil remedy described in edu-returned-check-remedies-nv. Money-order question (118A.303(1)(a)) UNRESOLVED: no appellate authority or official guidance; landlord-side counsel (Karsaz Law, 2025-10-01) calls "landlord-imposed fees only" the prevailing reading, while Legal Aid Center of Southern Nevada material lists "a check or money order" as a free method - a conflict between secondary sources. The clause stays drafted to be lawful on either reading. Karsaz also reports courts adding a 118A.303-noncompliance checkbox to the Tenant Affidavit form - i.e. it is being raised as an eviction defense.

title: Rent Increase Notice
bodyText: Landlord will not increase the Monthly Rent unless Landlord serves Tenant with written notice at least 60 days in advance of the first rental payment to be increased or, for any periodic tenancy of less than one month, at least 30 days in advance. During the Term, the Monthly Rent will not be increased except as this Lease expressly provides.
notes: NV: Section-open read of revisor text (leg.state.nv.us, Rev. 4/15/2026). NRS 118A.300 (A. 1983, 2021). 60 days; 30 for periodic tenancy < 1 month. No frequency or amount cap located in 118A. 118A.510 (retaliatory rent increase) text not yet read in official form. Rent-control preemption: not checked (outside 118A). | NV (text batch 2, 2026-09-24): NRS 118A.510 now read: a rent increase in retaliation for protected activity is barred, but an increase applied uniformly to all tenants is excepted (510(3)(d)).

title: Fire or Casualty Damage
bodyText: If the property is damaged or destroyed by fire or casualty to an extent that Tenant's enjoyment of it is substantially impaired, Landlord may terminate this Lease, and Tenant may, in addition to any other remedy: (a) immediately vacate and notify Landlord within 7 days afterward of Tenant's intention to terminate, in which case this Lease terminates as of the date Tenant vacated; or (b) if continued occupancy is lawful, vacate any part rendered unusable, in which case Rent is reduced in proportion to the reduction in fair rental value or lack of use. If this Lease terminates, Landlord will return all prepaid Rent and any recoverable Security Deposit, with Rent accounted for as of the date the property was vacated. This Section does not apply if the fire or casualty was caused by the deliberate or negligent act of Tenant, a member of Tenant's household, or another person on the property with Tenant's consent.
notes: NV: Section-open read of revisor text (leg.state.nv.us, Rev. 4/15/2026). NRS 118A.400 (A. 2021). Same URLTA architecture as fire-casualty-termination-ks but the tenant's notice window is 7 days (KS 5) and NV expressly gives the LANDLORD a termination right - cannot share the KS row.

title: Property Left After Tenancy
bodyText: If Tenant abandons the property or leaves personal property on it after an eviction or the end of the rental period, Landlord will reasonably provide for the safe storage of that property for 30 days and may charge the reasonable and actual costs of inventory, moving and storage before releasing it to Tenant or Tenant's authorized representative within that period.
